title: Broncos Urged to Trade for $76 Million Super Bowl Champion
description: Denver Broncos are being urged to trade for Pro Bowl edge rusher and Super Bowl champion. The post Broncos Urged to Trade for $76 Million Super Bowl Champion appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
If you want to understand 1 thing about the public-facing comments of NFL general managers — what they say with a microphone in their face — it's that you shouldn't believe a word that comes out of their mouths.

That's why, when a report comes out that the Arizona Cardinals are not interested in trading Pro Bowl edge rusher and Super Bowl champion Josh Sweat, no right-thinking team that needs an edge rusher should pay attention to it.

No Super Bowl contender needs an edge rusher worse than the Denver Broncos do right now, with their own star, Jonathon Cooper, placed on the NFL commissioner's exempt list with no return in sight following a pair of offseason arrests.

The Broncos should at least kick the tires on a trade and dangle a 2027 or 2028 2nd-round pick in front of the Cardinals to see if they'll bite and give up Sweat — a player who has already proven he could be the difference in playing in a Super Bowl or watching from home.

The great thing about a possible trade for Sweat is that there's zero chance the value goes up from a 2nd-round pick in the next few weeks as teams start the regular season.

Even without Cooper, the Broncos are still probably going to be really, really good. Even with Sweat, the Cardinals are still going to be really, really bad. Trading for Sweat is a long play to make sure they can close out a season — something that didn't happen in 2025 with a home loss to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game.

While the Cardinals seem to be saying they won't trade Sweat, the more likely scenario is all of that talk is being done to drive up his trade value — cheap skate teams are likely throwing 3rd- and 4th-round picks at Arizona for Sweat right now.

"The Cardinals are telling interested teams they aren't planning to trade Sweat, and I believe that to be true," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote on Wednesday. "No team has won or lost any games yet. Sweat is an important part of the Cardinals' defense, and if they still plan to be competitive (as most teams do at this point), the right move is to keep him. They've already paid a $7.22 million option bonus for this year and owe him $9.78 million in base salary for the season … Arizona is going to continue to get calls. Though I believe the team doesn't want to trade him, I also know these things change. And if Arizona is out of it in late October and/or Sweat indicates he doesn't want to be there anymore, you'll hear his name ahead of the deadline."

Sweat, 6-foot-5 and 265 pounds, had 2.5 sacks for the Philadelphia Eagles in a 40-22 Super Bowl win over the Kansas City Chiefs in February 2025 and signed a 4-year, $76.4 million free agent contract with the Cardinals 1 month later.

In 2025, he had a career-high 12.0 sacks this season to go with 12 tackles for loss, 4 forced fumbles and 16 QB hits and started all 17 regular-season games.

Not making the Pro Bowl with those numbers did something to Sweat emotionally.

"I'm upset because there's only two individual things that you can get and it's Pro Bowl and All-Pro," Sweat told ESPN's Josh Weinfuss. "And I got one taken away from me. I'm just flat out saying it was taken away from me — and it ain't the first time … It's like I don't know what else I could have done at that point. I don't know what else I could have done. Now previous years, maybe you could have said he didn't have the popularity, maybe he didn't get the fan vote. This year, I was second in fan voting for NFC. It's like, what else did they want me to do?"

title: International equestrian body lifts ban on Russia
description: The International Equestrian Federation lifts its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.
fullText:
The International Equestrian Federation has lifted its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.

Riders, horses and officials from Russia and Belarus have been prohibited from representing their countries under their national flags at FEI events since March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

The international governing body will also allow events to be held in Russia as part of regulations that will come into effect on 5 October.

The move means participants from Russia and Belarus will no longer be required to compete as Neutral Individual Athletes.

The FEI's decision comes after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced in June that it would provisionally lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee.

It means athletes from the region could potentially be cleared to represent Russia at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

Following its announcement, the FEI said it would like to "take this opportunity to reiterate its support for the people of Ukraine".

title: 'NRL investment in Super League benefits both parties'
description: Incoming St Helens boss Kevin Walters says National Rugby League investment in the Super League would benefit both parties.
fullText:
Australia and incoming St Helens head coach Kevin Walters has backed a potential partnership between Super League and the National Rugby League (NRL).

Last month Super League clubs rejected a £35m investment offer from the Australian Rugby League Commission, which plans to help grow the European competition's revenue.

Talks over a potentially game-changing deal have been ongoing since last year, but a fresh offer is yet to be made.

"I don't think Super League is in need of help, that's not what I see", Walters told BBC Sport.

"But I do see a great partnership between the NRL and Super League [and] I feel that will benefit both parties.

"There's so many Australian and New Zealand players playing in the Super League…it's been a great competition and the NRL…reaching out and offering some support, and also possibly some sort of ownership, would be beneficial for the game."

In July the NRL struck a new seven-year broadcast deal worth around £400 million annually to its clubs.

"The game is very rich now in the NRL, so I can't see why that wouldn't transfer into Super League as well", said Walters.

"The new broadcast deal smashed all sorts of records, so it's nothing but a positive if the NRL can get involved in Super League. Both competitions will benefit highly."

Walters was speaking during a short trip to St Helens, the club he will join after leading hosts and holders Australia into the World Cup next month. Saints chairman Eamonn McManus has said that the NRL and Super League should be working together to help grow the game as a global sport - instead of one organisation taking over from the other, insisting it is "not a matter of picking at a carcass, taking over a weak sport."

The RFL has said it is "genuinely interested in exploring a mutually beneficial and financially fair partnership with the NRL, which we firmly believe would unlock the significant added value benefit of creating a single global entity for the sport."

A former head coach at NRL side Brisbane Broncos, Walters guided the Kangaroos to a 3-0 win over England in last year's Ashes tour.

When asked how much of a gap there was between the two leagues, he said: "Physically there's no gap. It's just possibly a little bit of the speed of the game, but the talent is certainly here. It's a very strong competition and very well respected in Australia. Ask some of our players how tough those games were…it was a tough series."

Eleven NRL stars have been named in England's preliminary World Cup squad, and Walters believes he can help stem the drain of talent from the Super League to Australia.

"Certainly that will be part of my mantra, to keep our best players here. One of the attractions of the NRL is you know you're playing against some of the best players in the world. The second one is the financial rewards. I feel like Super League can can lift its numbers financially for player reward…and if [it is] more rewarding here, I think more more players will stay.

"I've watched a lot of World Cups in the last 30 years, and this one will be the most competitive of all...I feel the English side will be as strong as it's ever been."

Super League 'not a carcass to be picked at' - McManus

'We're not arrogant' - NRL chief says Super League talent will not be drained

Having won four consecutive Super League titles between 2019 and 2022, Saints have suffered a decline since, finishing third, sixth and fifth in the table over the past three seasons. They have also endured a torrid current campaign, with injuries heavily contributing to them being in danger of missing the Super League play-offs for the first time.

"This has been a great club for a long time" said Walters. "It feels a bit surreal for me to be the next coach of Saints next year. It feels good.

"I wouldn't say it's fallen a long way. It's fallen off its perch a little bit, but that's not to suggest it's not fixable. I feel very confident if we get the right people involved in the club we can get success very quickly."

When asked how big an overhaul was required, Walters added: "Not reconstruction…it's just a little bit of tinkering of some players and staff, and I feel like we can get on the right path pretty quickly. My first senior coaching job at the Brisbane Broncos, they finished last, and within three years we got to a Grand Final, so this to me is not as big a task.

"The history that this club has was very appealing. It just felt right the right decision."

title: Celtic loan keeper Johnstone & teenage Chelsea duo Mheuka & Emenalo
description: Celtic complete loan deals for former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone and teenage Chelsea duo Shumaira Mheuka and Landon Emenalo.
fullText:
Celtic have completed loan deals for former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone and teenage Chelsea duo Shumaira Mheuka and Landon Emenalo.

Johnstone, 33, arrives from Wolverhampton Wanderers and will provide competition for Finland international Viljami Sinisalo.

Striker Mheuka, 18, has extended his contract at Chelsea until 2031, having made nine outings for the London club.

Four of those came in the 2024-25 Conference League, including his only start. Last season, he captained the Chelsea Under-21 side, scoring 18 goals in 19 games.

Emenalo, 18, also joins on loan from the London club and will offer cover for Kieran Tierney at left-back.

He made 14 Premier League two appearances for Chelsea's Under-21 team last season and set up three goals in those outings.

Johnstone, who won the last of his four England caps in 2023, made 17 appearances last season but lost his starting place at relegated Wolves in December and has not played since an FA Cup loss to Liverpool in early March.

"I'm buzzing to be here and I'm excited to get going," said the goalkeeper, who began his career at Manchester United and has had spells at Aston Villa, West Bromwich Albion and Crystal Palce.

"I didn't need convincing by anyone, but Joe Hart rang me the other day just to reiterate what a place this is, what a great group of lads and how the fans are unbelievable.

"You hear about the size of the club, but just being here for a day, you notice how big the club is. And the pressure to win, which is what I like – pressure to win, pressure to perform and we all want to win trophies."

Kasper Schmeichel had been first choice at Celtic since the summer of 2024, but played his last game in February and subsequently retired due to a shoulder injury.

Manager Martin O'Neill said Johnstone would be "a very good addition" and that Mheuka has "great quality".

O'Neill also said new left-back Emenalo "has many attributes which I think can benefit us", adding he is "very quick on the ball and, while he can defend, he certainly gets up the pitch into attacking positions too."

title: Norris sets up junior team to help drivers to F1
description: World champion Lando Norris is setting up his own junior team to support young drivers on their route to Formula 1.
fullText:
World champion Lando Norris says he is putting his own money into setting up a driver development programme and his own team so he can "try to find the next true Formula 1 champion".

Norris' team, to be known as LN4 Fusion, launched on Wednesday on the eve of the Italian Grand Prix weekend. It will run teams across multiple feeder categories starting from next year.

Norris said he wanted to put something back into motorsport after the success he has achieved.

"Why? Because I can," he told BBC Sport in an exclusive interview.

"I have the amazing opportunity to use the bonuses of what was my dream, use the people that I've met, the teams that I've been with and kind of all put it into a big bowl and try and help kind of give back and re-share it with other people and help other people achieve their dream.

"And that's something that almost excites me just as much as saying I wanted to achieve it myself, you know, over the last few years.

"So the fact I can help other people out, that's something I think that's just a beautiful thing in life when you get to do it. And especially if I can do it within the world of motorsport."

How to follow Italian Grand Prix on the BBC

Slow start makes me want to stay - Norris extends McLaren deal to 2030

Norris said he had "double-ticked" his childhood dreams of getting to Formula 1 and becoming champion, and that this new project "means something and sets a fire inside of me".

He added: "With the Legacy programme first, it's just a perfect opportunity for me to try and give back and support people.

"I know how fortunate I was growing up, having just great opportunities all the time. I know how lucky I was to always be in that position.

"For me, so many things stem from giving. It's what I love to do with my friends, you know, and always take them on holidays and use the bonuses of my job and my life and share it all with them.

"And now I get to do it not only from a personal side with my friends and things, but get to help other drivers, young coming through. To say that and it's even cooler in some ways to help someone else to do that.

"It's a perfect combination. I get to support some drivers I can support. I have timed it so by the time I retire, they are old enough and can take my seat!"

Norris will be in overall charge of the programme but has signed a team of leaders to run it for him while he races full time in F1.

"From a driver development and the legacy programme, I don't think it's something that takes a lot of time.

"It can be a day here or a day there or not even that. It can be a phone call or a text from the drivers that I'm working with saying, can you help me here or do you have any guidance here or whatever it is, you know. So that's not something that takes time.

"That's just a thing that I'm happily willing to do. Everyone knows my focus is still on Formula One. That's my job and that's where all of my focus will be.

"I have a lot of faith and I believe very strongly in the people that we have running the different projects in the day-to-day. And in a way, I feel like I can step back and do nothing and things can still roll on and take place.

"But I want to be a part of it and I want to help in any way I can."

LN4 Fusion will be run by Rene Rosin, founder and former boss of Prema, one of the most successful teams in the junior categories over the past two decades.

In parallel, Norris is setting up what is described as "an independent, fully funded driver development" scheme, to be called the LN4 Legacy Programme.

"I've been really lucky to have some amazing people around me throughout my career, and I know that getting to Formula 1 takes so much more than just talent," Norris said.

"You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time.

"That's what these two projects are all about. LN4 Fusion is about building a race team that can compete with the best in junior motorsport, with great people and a great environment for drivers to develop.

"The LN4 Legacy Programme is about helping talented young drivers get opportunities they might not otherwise have."

Norris' programme will run teams in the Italian F4 Championship, FIA Formula Regional European Championship and FIA Formula 3 Championship in 2027.

The aim is also to compete in Formula 2 next year, but the application process for that has not yet been completed.

Norris will be co-owner of the project along with an investment group run by businessman Dan Richards, who has a background in technology.

The main headquarters of the programme will be in Veneto, Italy.

The UK arm, led by Dan Hazlewood, head of the Fusion Motorsport karting team, will be based in Cambridgeshire and run a programme in British F4.

The young driver programme will be run by Julian Rouse, who was formerly head of a similar programme for the Alpine F1 team.

Richards said: "What we have created is far more than simply the acquisition of a racing team.

"We have assembled a rare combination and secured the right sporting leadership in the industry: an established operation, a Formula 1 world champion, the most successful team principal in junior single-seater racing over the past two decades, world-class motorsport expertise, significant investment and a shared ambition to build a team capable of competing at the highest levels of the sport."

Rosin said: "Having Lando on board adds a further dimension to this project. He has come through the junior single-seater ranks and understands its demands. His involvement will make a real difference to the team."

title: Summer off England duty took me by surprise - Itoje
description: England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially taken aback by the suggestion he step away from international action for the July Tests
fullText:
England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially shocked when head coach Steve Borthwick raised the possibility of him taking the summer off.

Itoje missed England's matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, holidaying in Mauritius and Nigeria as he took a first proper summer break from professional rugby in more than a decade.

The 31-year-old, whose mother died in the weeks before he led England through a deflating Six Nations campaign that featured just one win, says he is now feeling the benefits of his time away.

"I spoke to Steve Borthwick two weeks after the Six Nations and at the end of a long conversation he mentioned we would have to think about what to do in the summer," Itoje told Rugby Union Weekly.

"I was taken aback a bit - it wasn't something that was in my mind.

"At the end of the season it is just the done thing to go on tour.

"But once I had digested it and had thought about it, the more I thought about it, the more I thought it was the best thing for me.

"I'm not annoyed by it at all. It was a wise and prudent decision, it has given me the best opportunity to perform well over the next period of time."

Itoje made his England debut in 2016 and has won 102 caps, as well as touring three times with the British and Irish Lions.

He played more than 30 matches in each of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns, breaching the recommended limit of 2,400 match minutes in the former and narrowly avoiding doing so in the latter.

"I would argue that the mental recovery was far more significant than physically," he said.

"I feel like I'm in a good physical condition, but mentally it was a heavy, busy year, both personally and professionally. So, it was nice to have just a bit of time to take a breath."

Itoje bumped into the England squad at Heathrow Airport as their return from a defeat by the Springboks in Johannesburg coincided with his own from Nigeria.

"I was on the shuttle train back to baggage reclaim and looked to my right and there was [Saracens and England team-mate] Jamie George, I looked to my left and there was Steve Borthwick, and they both looked at me in disbelief," he added.

Apart from that coincidence, Itoje kept his distance from the England set-up over the summer, sending the squad the odd good luck message, but opting against watching their games live.

"It was difficult to do, but when you're supposed to take a break, then if you're living and breathing every moment of a game..." he said.

"I watched them back in retrospect [knowing the final score], partly because I wanted to remove some of the emotion from watching it.

"That's the beauty of live sport - when you watch a game, you're in every nook and cranny, every tackle.

"But that also probably has a hidden emotional weight. The whole purpose of the rest was to get back on the even keel, so that was my methodology."

Itoje's rest precedes another busy period in his life.

Saracens' Prem season begins away to Leicester on 27 September before England take on Australia, Japan, New Zealand and a final's weekend play-off opponent in November's conclusion to the Nations Championship.

And the start of the Rugby World Cup in Australia is a little over a year away.

Meanwhile, his wife Mimi is expecting the couple's first child - a boy - imminently.

"I am very excited," Itoje added

"I want a minimum of three children, I don't really have a maximum.

"My cousin's grandfather must have 60 kids, but that isn't a route I am going down!"

title: Northern Ireland boss O'Neill 'hopeful' training centre plans progress
description: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says that he is "certainly hopeful" that the Irish Football Association can move forward with plans to have a National Training Centre open by 2028.
fullText:
Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill said that he was "certainly hopeful" that the Irish Football Association can move forward with plans to have a national training centre open by 2028.

The IFA announced in February 2025 their plans for the "state-of-the-art" facility which will be located next to the Galgorm Resort just outside of Ballymena and will have "world-class pitches and cutting-edge training facilities".

The association reiterated their desire to proceed with the proposal last month, but did say they hope to "mitigate concerns where possible" after objections from local residents.

O'Neill, who grew up in Ballymena, believes having the facility at Galgorm will have a positive impact on the town.

"It's important that you do have a national training centre that kids are used to coming to from a young age. It's an elite facility that shows the intent from the association as they continue to develop players," he told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

"We have a young team at the minute, which we've developed through the JD academy and it's something we should be very proud of, but the national training centre is importantly to the development not just of the senior team but the underage teams and the women's team.

"I'm certainly hopeful, I'm not in a position of granting authority on these things but it would be good for the town. It can only enhance the town and hopefully the project continues to progress."

IFA 'steadfast' in vision for new training centre

Irish FA announces National Training Centre at Galgorm

Looking ahead to the upcoming Nations League campaign, O'Neill also said that he does not expect Liverpool right back Conor Bradley to feature as he continues his recovery from a knee injury sustained in January.

Northern Ireland face Georgia, Hungary and Ukraine in Group B2 across six games in September, October and November, but O'Neill believes a more realistic return date for Bradley for his country will be the 2027 March international break.

"I'm comfortable with that," O'Neill said when asked if he was resigned to the fact that Bradley would not feature in the campaign.

"If we see him this side of Christmas it's a real bonus, if not, we look forward to March.

"Conor is where I expected him to be. I knew the injury was going to take longer than some people were thinking. He's making good progress. It has to be managed very carefully an injury of that nature," O'Neill added.

"Conor will be with us when he's ready and fit and we'll be delighted to have him back."

title: Wrist injury to keep Hadjar out of Italian GP
description: Red Bull will be without Isack Hadjar at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix as he continues to recover from a wrist injury.
fullText:
Red Bull will be without Isack Hadjar for a second consecutive race, with the Frenchman set to miss this weekend's Italian Grand Prix as he continues to recover from a wrist injury he sustained during the summer.

Hadjar, 21, missed last month's Dutch Grand Prix and will once again be replaced by New Zealander Liam Lawson in Monza.

Lawson, who normally races for Red Bull's second team, Racing Bulls, will compete alongside Max Verstappen this weekend - after finishing seventh last time.

Lawson's spot at Racing Bulls will once again be filled by reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda.

On Wednesday, Red Bull said Hadjar - who broke his wrist while boxing - was making "encouraging progress" and that the team would not be taking any "unnecessary risks" with his return to competition.

Red Bull are fourth in the constructors' championship standings, behind Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren.

title: Britain's Brennan claims third Vuelta stage win
description: Britain's Matthew Brennan powers to his third win at the Vuelta a Espana in a sprint finish on stage 11.
fullText:
Britain's Matthew Brennan sprinted to his third win at the 2026 Vuelta a Espana on Wednesday has he powered to victory on stage 11.

The 21-year-old Visma-Lease a Bike rider easily held off Frenchman Bryan Coquard and Belgium's Jordi Meeus at the climax of the 153.8km route from Cartagena to Lorca.

Overall leader Enric Mas of Spain retained the red jersey and has a one minute and 18-second lead over Slovenia's Primoz Roglic in the general classification, with Britain's Oscar Onley just over a further minute back in fourth.

Brennan held up three fingers after he crossed the line to celebrate a trio of victories in an impressive first Grand Tour.

"I'm with a team full of massive champions," said Brennan, who was also victorious in the second and fifth stages.

"You've got guys who have been on podiums in Grand Tours and won them as well, and you've also got guys who have won big classics in some huge races.

"The boys did a fantastic job within that last 10km to really keep us in the right place, in the right position, out of trouble. And we crossed the line first, so we're super happy."

Lidl-Trek's Mads Pedersen pulled out of the predominantly flat stage, earmarked as a day for the sprinters, through illness.

Thursday's 12th stage sees riders travel 166.6km in the mountains from Vera, facing five categorised climbs, including the double climb of Velefique and the Calar Alto summit finish.

title: Olympic champion Davis-Woodhall 'lucky to be alive' after car crash
description: Olympic long jump champion Tara Davis-Woodhall says she is "lucky and blessed to be alive" after being involved in a car crash.
fullText:
Olympic long jump champion Tara Davis-Woodhall says she is "lucky and blessed to be alive" after being involved in a car crash.

The 27-year-old American was on her way to training last week when she was involved in a "very scary" head-on collision, leaving her with a "severe" concussion.

While not ruling herself out of this month's inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest, the reigning world champion says she has been unable to train since the accident.

"Luckily I walked away without any major injuries," Davis-Woodhall wrote on social media.

"At this point I'm working with my team and doctors to get healthy, but I'm not sure if I will be ready to compete at Ultimate Championships next week. More updates to come."

Davis-Woodhall said her injuries were not life-threatening but that both cars, which were going at about 20mph, were written off.

"It's really unfortunate timing; I am at the peak of my training right now," she said.

"I'm as fast as I've ever been. I'm as strong as I've ever been. So this decision is very difficult for me. I don't know where I am right now."

The championships in Hungary start on 11 September, where athletes will compete for a top prize of £111,000.

The competition brings together Olympic, world and Diamond League champions, as well as the year's leading performers in a three-day end-of-season event.

Davis-Woodhall won long jump gold at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, before winning the Worlds in Tokyo a year later.

title: Locals torch migrant shelters as Spain's PM points blame beyond the border
description: Ceuta residents burned migrant shelters as Pedro Sánchez accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks of spreading disinformation that fueled the crisis.
fullText:
Residents in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta tore down and burned makeshift migrant shelters amid escalating tensions over a massive influx from neighboring Morocco, as Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks of helping spread disinformation that fueled the crisis.

Demonstrators carrying Spanish flags moved toward beachside migrant camps last week, destroying shelters and setting fires as police attempted to keep protesters and migrants apart, according to Spain's public broadcaster RTVE and news agency EFE. Protesters chanted "Invasores, expulsión" — "Invaders, expulsion" — as they advanced toward the beaches where migrants have been staying, EFE reported Aug. 27.

Hundreds of residents returned to the streets the following day, marching toward the Trampolín and Benítez beach areas where migrants were camped and repeating the same chant, according to EFE.

The unrest follows an unprecedented surge on July 30 and 31, when more than 72,000 migrants irregularly crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, one of the European Union's two land borders with Africa. At least 100 people died attempting the crossing, according to Ceuta authorities cited by Reuters on Aug. 31. Roughly 5,000 migrants remained in the enclave as of Monday.

State Department Raises Travel Warning For Part Of Spain As Migrant Surge Sparks Military Deployment

Sánchez on Monday directly linked the mass crossing to what he described as a foreign-backed disinformation campaign.

Spanish authorities have said misleading videos and posts circulating on Instagram, TikTok and other social-media platforms falsely suggested that migrants who reached Ceuta by sea would be permitted to remain in Spain.

Ceuta Migrant Surge Exposes Spain-morocco Tensions As Islamist Groups Reportedly Seek To Exploit Border Crisis

Sánchez told radio station SER that research by the European Union's diplomatic service, the European External Action Service, indicated Russian and Israeli networks had participated in spreading the disinformation alongside far-right networks, Reuters reported Aug. 31.

He argued that Russia and Israel had seized on the crisis to attack Madrid because of disagreements with his government over the wars in Ukraine and Gaza.

However, Sánchez provided no further details about the evidence supporting the accusation, according to the reports.

Both governments rejected his claims.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Sánchez of "lying shamelessly" and said in a post on X that the Spanish leader was attempting to divert attention from domestic policy failures.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov separately rejected Spain's accusation that Russia was connected to the Ceuta migration crisis.

Sánchez also rejected allegations that Morocco's government deliberately facilitated the border surge, telling SER, "When people talk and speculate about the participation of Moroccan authorities, I deny this outright," according to Reuters. Spanish opposition parties and some human-rights organizations have accused Rabat of allowing the crossings, an allegation Morocco denies.

Spanish Journalist Says Ceuta Residents Believe Government Isn't Doing Enough To Prevent Another Migrant Rush

The disinformation surrounding the Ceuta crossing had been building well before Sánchez publicly accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks. Fox News Digital reported Aug. 4 that an open-source investigation by Golden Owl Intelligence traced weeks of activity across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that circulated misleading interpretations of Spanish immigration law, along with information about routes, meeting points and recommended crossing times.

The campaign intensified after Spain's Supreme Court issued a July 8 ruling restricting the immediate return of migrants intercepted at sea near Ceuta and Melilla. Simplified accounts of the ruling, combined with confusion over Spain's separate plan to regularize hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants, were circulated online as evidence that migrants reaching Spanish territory would be allowed to stay.

Spain's Migrant Surge Reignites Debate Over Europe's Islamist Terror Threat

Zineb Riboua, a research fellow at the Hudson Institute, said at the time that Islamist movements were also seeking to exploit the crisis politically. Riboua argued that Islamist voices in Morocco and Spain were amplifying the unrest and portraying Europe as an attractive destination while using Morocco's ties with Israel and the U.S. to attack the Moroccan government. In a July 31 analysis, Riboua wrote that Islamist activists had spent years encouraging young Moroccans to believe their country offered them little future and depicting Europe as a place where prosperity and opportunity were easily available.

The crisis has also spread beyond Spain. Italy on Monday extended for another 15 days its suspension of Schengen free-movement arrangements with Spain, a step first imposed July 31 in response to the mass influx into Ceuta.

Nile Gardiner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, warned Fox News Digital at the outset of the crisis that Ceuta could become "a key turning point in the unraveling of the European Union." "Once you unravel Schengen — which I think is inevitable — this breaks down the entire European project," Gardiner said.

title: Police chief fired amid controversy in aftermath of child's shooting in a small Mississippi city
description: The police chief of a northern Mississippi city where 1-year-old Black child Kohen Wiley was shot and killed by police responding to a shoplifting call was fired Tuesday amid a new controversy.  Senat...
fullText:
The police chief of a northern Mississippi city where 1-year-old Black child Kohen Wiley was shot and killed by police responding to a shoplifting call was fired Tuesday amid a new controversy.

Senatobia Police Chief Harold Vanderford submitted his resignation the same day, but the city's board of aldermen declined to acknowledge it and instead voted unanimously to fire the chief, according to the city clerk, who did not elaborate on their reasons.

The firing followed reporting by The New York Times, Mississippi Today and Verite News last month that alleged Vanderford used racist slurs in private text conversations with a colleague. It also comes amid the aftermath of the child's shooting and other incidents.

Kohen was fatally shot and another woman was wounded June 14 after a Senatobia police officer fired into a vehicle while investigating a shoplifting call at a Walmart. The toddler's mother, Vellesiya Wiley, denied that she or a friend accompanying her had stolen anything, and no charges have been filed against them.

Kohen was Black, as is his mother. The death ignited anger in a small city where tensions between Black residents and the police have boiled over in recent years. Senatobia, with a population of more than 8,000, is about 40 miles (65 kilometers) south of Memphis.

"I believe the Board has a responsibility to protect the integrity and trust of the Senatobia Police Department," Alderman Demetrius Garrett wrote in a Facebook post. "I still believe in unity. But unity does not mean ignoring serious issues it means standing together for what is right."

The city had previously addressed the reporting about Vanderford's texts, saying in a statement on Aug. 25 that he had appeared before the mayor and board to answer questions and that he would continue to serve as police chief.

Senatobia Alderman Chris McConnell called for an independent investigation of the police department.

"We need answers about departmental leadership, internal culture, the handling of complaints and misconduct, financial practices, and whether the Board has been receiving the information necessary to provide proper oversight," McConnell said in a statement. "Our citizens deserve a police department they can trust."

National civil rights attorney Ben Crump, representing Kohen's family, called the chief's firing the "right decision."

"The racist language that cost Chief Vanderford his job is exactly why this family cannot simply be told to trust the process," Crump said in a statement calling for the Mississippi Bureau of Investigations to release body-camera footage of the shooting. "Give this family the facts they have been owed since the day Kohen died."

The Senatobia Police Department declined to comment on the firing.

Vanderford was appointed police chief on Sept. 29, 2025, after the board of aldermen declined to reappoint the previous chief, Richard Chandler, in July of that year.

Chandler led the police department through several controversies. They included the 2023 arrest of a 10-year-old Black boy for urinating in public and an incident in which an officer threatened a woman with a Taser and pulled her from her car during a dispute over a handicapped parking space outside the same Walmart where Kohen was shot.

"You removed Richard Chandler," said Senatobia community activist Patrick Lumumba. "But you did not remove the culture of racism, and that's what Vanderford harbors."

Following the child's death, Lumumba formed the Senatobia Committee for Accountability and Transparency, a community watchdog group that is demanding answers about the June shooting and advocating for better policing.

He voiced confidence in Lt. Angelica Maze, who will serve as the department's interim police chief, calling her a"good person."

title: Uber drivers launch European class action over ‘soulless’ and ‘scary’ AI algorithm
description:
Landmark lawsuit claims tech company’s pay-setting system has breached privacy laws and pushed down earnings
Uber drivers have launched a landmark legal action against the ride-hailing company claiming they live in “constant fear” of a “soulless” algorithm it uses to set pay and allocate jobs.
Drivers from the UK, the Netherlands and other countries have joined the compensation claim that could run into billions of dollars. It alleges an AI-powered pay-setting system breaches data protection laws and pushes down their earnings.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Landmark lawsuit claims tech company’s pay-setting system has breached privacy laws and pushed down earnings

Uber drivers have launched a landmark legal action against the ride-hailing company claiming they live in “constant fear” of a “soulless” algorithm it uses to set pay and allocate jobs.

Drivers from the UK, the Netherlands and other countries have joined the compensation claim that could run into billions of dollars. It alleges an AI-powered pay-setting system breaches data protection laws and pushes down their earnings.

The claim has been filed at Amsterdam’s district court, where the $150bn (£111bn) San Francisco tech company has its European HQ. It is the first collective legal move of its kind, according to the European Trade Union Confederation.

The case centres on an opaque “black box” algorithm fed on information about drivers, which sets a personalised rate for each ride. Drivers fear it pushes down fares to the minimum they are willing to accept.

Drivers have told the Guardian the algorithm has offered the same job to different people at different pay rates and offers them less for a return journey after a long trip because it calculates they will not want to come home empty.

“It is like someone watching you all the time and knowing about your weakness – the boss is the algorithm,” said Mohammed Shirwa, a 41-year-old Uber driver in Rotterdam. “All the time the algorithm is learning about you and what you are willing to accept. So the prices go low but you are stuck. It knows you need the job.”

Kola Oba, who calls the algorithm “soulless”, was taking a break in Tottenham, north London, with another driver when they were offered the same job.

The other driver was offered £27 and Oba was offered £23. The pair suspected it was because Oba, 48, had taken several cheap jobs and the AI assumed he would accept a lower price. Uber has previously said such discrepancies were down to other features of its system including GPS, surge pricing, promotions and testing.

“It’s scary – they have all my information and they are using it against my own wellbeing,” Oba said. “It defines how much I earn, how long I have to work, my time with my family, my resting time.”

AI models take an increasing role in assigning work to humans by using their rapidly increasing power to learn about a business’s needs and staff behaviour and then acting as a “synthetic manager”.

The Dutch data protection authority fined ⁠Uber €825m (£708m) last month for deactivating driver ⁠accounts through automated systems without ​adequate notice. Uber said it would appeal. The company is also planning to roll out driverless cars in European cities from London to Zagreb, initially with human supervisions.

The legal case is being led by the Worker Info Exchange, a campaign group whose founder, James Farrar, secured a UK supreme court ruling that Uber drivers should have worker rights.

Relating to about 241,000 drivers across the EU and the UK, the claim alleges that Uber has unlawfully used automated decision-making, including profiling, in dynamically setting pay and allocating work.

The lawsuit, which also claims the company unlawfully used driver data to train its AI models, is seeking damages for affected drivers and an injunction to halt the conduct which it claims breaches GDPR data regulations.

The drivers claim Uber has operated dynamic pay-setting in the UK since 2023, pushing down their annual incomes by about £5,000. The system was introduced in the Netherlands this year.

Uber’s chief executive, Dara Khosrowshahi, said in 2023: “I think that what we can do better is targeting of different trips to different drivers based on their preferences or based on behavioural patterns that they’re showing us.”

Uber said it did not adjust the price offered for a trip based on an individual driver’s behaviour and that a history of accepting or rejecting trips was not used to personalise pay offers. Instead, it said, dynamic pricing allowed it to increase pay on less attractive trips, boosting a driver’s earning potential.

“While we haven’t seen the claim yet, we categorically reject the allegations,” an Uber spokesperson said. “The Uber app uses real-time information about the trip such as journey, duration and destination to calculate fares.

“Drivers see their earnings and where a trip is going before they decide whether to accept it. The vast majority of total fares continue to go where they belong: into drivers’ pockets, and the percentage that Uber keeps from fares has remained relatively flat.”

A 2025 study by academics at the University of Oxford, which Uber said relied on incomplete and selective data, found there had been substantial cuts in driver earnings after the “dynamic” algorithm was introduced.

Farrar said: “It’s bad enough that Uber’s dynamic pay algorithms have squeezed driver pay for years now but the intrusive and underhanded way in which Uber uses its technology to monitor and influence drivers’ behaviour is an affront to their dignity as workers and as human beings.”

Anton Ekker, a Dutch lawyer leading the case, said: “A computer algorithm should not independently make decisions that strip individuals of their livelihood. Like so many other online platforms, it should be held accountable for the large-scale exploitation of vulnerabilities of European citizens.”

title: New York City to ban student AI use in public schools until high school
description:
Teachers and parents have warned against AI use in schools over concerns of ‘cognitive surrender’
New York City will ban students’ use of artificial intelligence in public schools through eighth grade, typically age 13 or 14. The prohibition is scheduled to be announced on Wednesday and will go into effect next week.
The change is part of a sweeping overhaul of the use of technology in the US’s largest school district, which enrolls roughly 900,000 students a year. In another policy shift, classrooms will keep students off laptops or tablets through the third grade, age nine or 10. The city’s public school technology policies are closely watched by the rest of the United States.
fullText:
Teachers and parents have warned against AI use in schools over concerns of ‘cognitive surrender’

New York City will ban students’ use of artificial intelligence in public schools through eighth grade, typically age 13 or 14. The prohibition is scheduled to be announced on Wednesday and will go into effect next week.

The change is part of a sweeping overhaul of the use of technology in the US’s largest school district, which enrolls roughly 900,000 students a year. In another policy shift, classrooms will keep students off laptops or tablets through the third grade, age nine or 10. The city’s public school technology policies are closely watched by the rest of the United States.

Teachers and parents have warned against the use of AI instructional software in schools over concerns about harming children’s mental health and cognitive development, in particular an abdication of reasoning to software, a phenomenon researchers have dubbed “cognitive surrender”, as well as environmental damage.

AI use will only be allowed in high school, which begins in the ninth grade in the US school system. Even then, it will be limited to specific uses, such as learning about the technology itself.

AI “companion chatbots” offering psychological support will also be banned. The rules allow teachers to use AI for tasks including preparing lessons or writing messages, but they are forbidden from asking AI to grade assignments.

The city’s education department recommends limiting screen time to 45 minutes in class for middle schoolers – sixth through eighth grade – and 30 minutes for elementary school students. But the question remains of how to monitor AI use, since it often takes place outside the school environment.

The new rules follow an initial framework published in March, which used a traffic light system to determine which tasks AI would be used for. In 2023, the school system forbade students’ use of ChatGPT, though the ban was reversed less than a year later.

The 2026 framework, which allowed students to use AI for research, exploration and creative projects, sparked fury among many parents and teachers who considered it too lenient.

In response, the city’s schools chancellor, Kamar Samuels, said that leaders had “missed the mark” in their communications, adding his office would carefully review parents’ feedback for incorporation into future rules.

The city had long planned to follow the March framework with a more comprehensive “guidebook” to take feedback into account, the education department has said.

The department will set up a taskforce made up of teachers, elected officials, experts and union representatives. The taskforce is to produce a report in April, intended to serve as the basis for New York’s AI-in-schools policy.

fullText:
Judge declines to make Google sell AdX in win for firm against US antitrust enforcers’ attempts to break up big tech

Alphabet’s Google escaped a breakup of its advertising technology business on Wednesday, when a judge in Virginia ⁠rejected US antitrust enforcers’ bid to force a sale of Google’s online advertising exchange.

While the ad exchange is a small part of Google’s business, the ruling is the second powerful ⁠symbolic victory against the US Department ⁠of Justice in ​its efforts to force Google to sell assets to address illegal monopolies.

US judge Leonie Brinkema in Alexandria, Virginia, declined to make Google sell AdX, where publishers pay Google a ⁠20% fee to sell ads in auctions that happen instantly when users load websites. She accepted most of the parties’ proposed behavioral remedies.

The justice department and a broad coalition of states sued Google in 2023 over ⁠its dominance in markets for advertising technology used by online publishers and websites.

In April 2025, Brinkema ruled that Google holds ​illegal monopolies on servers that host publisher ads and ad ‌exchanges which sit between buyers and ‌sellers. Google unlawfully locked publishers on its ad server into using its AdX, the judge found.

The tech company’s anticompetitive conduct “substantially harmed ‌Google’s publisher customers, the competitive process, and, ultimately, consumers of information on the open web”, Brinkema said at the time.

At a trial last year on remedies in the case, the justice department argued that Google cannot be trusted to run AdX, given its past behavior.

Google argued that a forced sale would be technically difficult and result in a long and painful transition that would hurt customers. The company also sought to show the justice department’s demand was different from Google’s own previous offer ‌to sell AdX to end an EU antitrust investigation, which Reuters reported in 2024.

Ad Manager represented 4.1% of Google’s overall revenue and 1.5% of operating profit in 2020, according to Wedbush research and analysis of ​court documents. More recent figures were redacted from court documents.

The ruling is the third time in a row that a judge has rejected a bid by US antitrust enforcers to break up big tech in a crackdown that started during Donald Trump’s first term. It is likely to fuel questions about whether courts are up to the task of checking ⁠the industry’s unprecedented power over the US economy.

A federal judge in Washington last year rejected the ​Federal Trade Commission’s attempt to make Meta ​Platforms sell off Instagram and WhatsApp, saying the ​agency failed to prove that Meta holds a monopoly in a social media landscape that has shifted ​drastically since the case ‌was brought in 2020.

Likewise, ​another judge in Washington, ​who previously ruled that Google holds an illegal monopoly in online search, rejected the justice department’s bid to make the company sell its Chrome browser, citing rising competition from generative artificial intelligence companies such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

US antitrust cases against Amazon and Apple, which involve big smartphone and online retail markets, will not go to trial until 2027 at the earliest.

title: Map shows where the 2026 ‘super’ El Niño could bring lots of rain, extreme drought
description: Some forecasts indicate this year's El Niño may be the strongest ever recorded.
fullText:
(NEXSTAR) – A "super" El Niño is gaining strength as we speak. If the climate phenomenon continues building at this pace, it could become the strongest El Niño we've seen in more than 75 years.

Some forecasts indicate it may be the strongest El Niño ever recorded, said Dr. Jeffrey Shaman, senior vice dean and professor at the Columbia Climate School.

But what that means for weather this year depends on where you live. For some parts of the world, El Niño means more wet winter storms. In other places, it can create drought conditions.

A map created by Columbia University's Center for Climate Systems Research combines multiple models, taking into account this year's El Niño and other climate factors, to predict which places will see more rain and which areas will see less rain than usual from October to the end of the year.

Parts of the world that are shaded in green and blue have the highest chances of seeing above-normal precipitation this year. In the U.S., it's the southeastern states who have the highest likelihood – above a 70% chance – of more rain than normal.

On the other side of the spectrum are the places shown in yellow and brown. Those areas, like some of the northeastern U.S. states, are more likely to see below-normal precipitation. That could create or exacerbate drought conditions.

Other parts of the world, like Brazil and Southeast Asia, have a more dire El Niño-related drought forecast than the U.S.

The map above only shows rainfall predictions through the end of the year, but this super-charged El Niño is likely to stick with us through early 2027.

That's when it could start having a bigger effect on the West Coast of the U.S., bringing more rain to Southern California and keeping the Pacific Northwest a little drier. The Ohio Valley also tends to be on the dry side during an El Niño year.

Of course, none of these outcomes are a guarantee. "Even the strongest El Niño events do not lead to the typical impact everywhere, but stronger events can more significantly tilt the odds in favor of expected outcomes," the Climate Prediction Center said in a recent update.

There are other elements influencing our climate and weather patterns, like warming global temperatures.

"El Niño is not the only thing that affects these seasonal forecasts, but it is one of the big drivers of it," said Shaman. "It gives a lot of certainty to the forecast."

In its latest forecast, the Climate Prediction Center said the odds that this year's El Niño will reach the highest strength level – often called a "super" El Niño – are now higher than 90%. There's a 69% chance it grows into the strongest El Niño since 1950.

title: 2 Grand Canyon flooding victims photographed on hiking trip in days before deaths
description: John Giusti and Brent Rosenkranz, from Texas, posted selfies from the Grand Canyon before devastating flash flooding swept through the area on Saturday.
fullText:
The two victims whose remains were found after flash flooding swept through the Grand Canyon were seen photographed on the same trip prior to the deadly incident.

The families of Texas chiropractor John Giusti, 46, and martial artist Brent Rosenkranz, 42, identified them as the two people whose bodies were recovered, according to Hannah Barricks, a liaison for the families. She told The Associated Press that a third friend, Timothy Smith, 53, went on the trip with them and remains missing as of late Monday.

All three men had ties to Granbury, Texas, and their families said they planned "several days of hiking, camping, fishing and exploring together," the AP also reported. The men spoke to their families Thursday and found their campsite Friday at the bottom of the Grand Canyon, the three families said in a joint statement released earlier Monday through Barricks.

The devastating flash flooding on Saturday, Aug. 29, happened along Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the Colorado River near Phantom Ranch. The area has a set of historic dormitories, a canteen and a campground that is a popular stopover for river rafters and people hiking from one rim of the Grand Canyon to the other.

Grand Canyon Water Pipeline Damaged Again As Flooding Complicates Repairs

Incident Cmdr. Dave Black said searchers used night vision and other equipment to find people who needed rescuing during the deluge. By sunset Saturday, 45 people were rescued, and 37 others were evacuated Sunday.

Rangers referred to the park's permit system and checked vehicle license plates to track the number of missing people.

"As of right now, they have no reason to believe, from the tips we've been through so far, that there's anybody besides the one" missing person, Black said during a news conference Monday evening.

Hiker Daniel Evans told the AP that it rained several times before the worst 30-minute downpour Saturday afternoon. He had been planning to rest through the hot day and spend the night near the hard-hit Bright Angel Campground area.

Earlier, rangers told him it looked to be safe. Then, as the rain poured, they told him it was time to go. He said he thought of Nepal and the massive floods and landslides that poured down mountain valleys last week.

Beloved Texas Chiropractor Killed In Grand Canyon Flash Flood

"The entire time it was raining — the entire time I'm going through all this and packing — I'm just keeping my eyes upstream, just praying that a wall of water isn't coming toward us," Evans said.

Janet Giusti, the wife of John Giusti, wrote on a fundraising page that "John was living out a lifetime dream exploring the majesty of the Grand Canyon when tragedy struck."

"Beyond his practice, he was a man of electric energy and boundless passion — an avid runner, an enthusiast of fast cars, and a massive fan of comic books and legendary heroes," she added. "Yet out of all the titles he carried, his absolute favorite was being a devoted father to his three beautiful girls."

Rosenkranz had posted selfies from the Grand Canyon before the flooding, tagging Giusti and sharing his excitement about the grueling adventure ahead.

"Just arrived at the Grand Canyon. Will be hiking over 31 miles next four days with vertical change of over a mile," Rosenkranz wrote. "Carrying a 40 lb backpack. This should be an adventure!"

Tina Newberry, whose daughter co-owns the ATA Glen Rose martial arts location, said Giusti had been exploring the canyon with fellow "ATA fathers" Rosenkranz and Smith when disaster struck.

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and The Associated Press contributed to this report.
