title: Swing Changes Fail When Golfers Rush The Fix
description: Golf.com reports the biggest mistake after a swing change is reverting to old habits. Learn the fix to keep your new mechanics.
fullText:
Most golfers ruin a good swing change before it even sticks. They make one adjustment and expect instant perfection. When the ball doesn't fly straight on the first try, they panic. This reaction is the biggest mistake players make after a swing change, according to Golf.com. The desire to fix a bad shot immediately often leads to a total reversion to old habits. It creates a cycle of confusion that stops progress cold. Players forget that learning a new motor skill takes time and repetition. They try to force the new move while under pressure. This approach usually results in worse contact than before the change began.

The root of this problem lies in how the brain processes new movements. When a player makes a bad contact, the instinct is to save the shot. This instinct overrides the new technical thought process. Golf.com notes that players often fall into these old habits right after a swing change. The brain prefers the familiar path, even if it is flawed. It is much easier to swing the way it has always been done than to trust a new feeling. This is especially true when the stakes are high or the score is slipping. A player might feel the new move for a few holes. Then a bad lie or a tricky shot triggers the old muscle memory. The new swing gets abandoned in favor of the known bad habit. This happens because the player focuses on the outcome of the shot rather than the process of the swing. They try to control the ball instead of trusting their body to execute the new plan.

Fixing this issue requires a shift in mindset and patience. Players must accept that bad shots are part of the learning curve. Trusting the new mechanics is more important than the immediate result. Golf.com emphasizes that avoiding old habits is the key to success after a swing change. The player needs to focus on the feel of the new move, not just the ball flight. Consistency comes from repetition, not from perfecting every single shot. It is better to hit a bad shot with the new swing than a good shot with the old one. This distinction helps the brain build new neural pathways. The goal is to make the new movement automatic over time. Rushing this process only delays the final breakthrough. Players who stick with the change eventually see better results. They stop fighting their body and start working with it.

Next time you see a player struggle after a tweak, look for the return of old patterns. It is a common struggle for amateurs and pros alike. The real test is whether they stick to the plan. Fans should expect some rough patches as players adjust. The ones who survive this phase are the ones who improve their game. Patience is the only real shortcut to a better swing.

title: Frank Warren gives major Anthony Joshua contract update with Tyson Fury in location limbo
description: Warren says Fury is signed and ready to fight regardless of the location with Madison Square Garden looking the most likely venue
fullText:
Frank Warren says that Anthony Joshua is yet to sign the contract for an all-British blockbuster fight with Tyson Fury as the wait goes on for an official announcement.

Fury suggested on Tuesday that confirmation of the hotly-anticipated showdown was close, posting a mocked-up image of himself facing off with Joshua above the words "New York City" on Instagram.

The expectation is that the bout will be hosted at the world-famous Madison Square Garden, as is the desire of Turki Alalshikh and Saudi state-owned promotional company Sela, though Joshua's camp prefer Wembley Stadium as the venue, which would allow for the element of a home crowd.

Warren, however, says that location is no longer a factor for Fury who has penned a contract that does not hinge on where the fight takes place, with the Queensberry chief insisting that "The Gypsy King" is now just waiting on Joshua's signature.

"The latest is Joshua's not signed yet," Warren said.

"It's not for me to give him [a deadline], it's the people who are paying the money. It's all this stuff, as I said from the beginning, it's about contracts. I know what the contracts say. The contracts have all got to be amended.

"Tyson's signed. Tyson's done. He don't care when the fight takes place. [If] they want it in New York, they want it in Barbados, they want it on the Isle of Wight, he's signed. He's done."

Warren also added that Fury signed up for the "AJ" fight as early as the beginning of this year, with plans originally being for the pair to fight in this month.

However, Joshua's involvement in car crash that took the lives of two of his close friends last December forced the date of fight night to be rearranged.

Both men have since had warm-up fights back, with Fury beating Arslanbek Makhmudov by decision in April before stopping Mariusz Wach in Thailand in July, while Joshua survived a scare to beat Kristian Prenga that same month.

"He signed for the fight in January," Warren continued. "The fight was supposed to take place in September, but what happened with AJ and his accident, that all got pushed back.

"Where we got to with it was obviously AJ had his fight back and we'd already had that one in December with Jake Paul.

"Then, it was decided to put it on in November. But one contract says one venue, the other contract says another venue, and the TV contract says another venue. I don't do the contracts."

title: Jaylen Brown Donates 2027 Nissan Sentra With Influencer To Single Mom Of 4
description: Jaylen Brown teamed up with MD Motivator to surprise a single mother of four with a brand-new Nissan Sentra.
fullText:
Philadelphia 76ers' Jaylen Brown helped deliver a massive surprise, which could probably be life-changing to a single mother of four, teaming up with popular social media influencer Zachary Dereniowski to gift a brand-new 2027 Nissan Sentra.

Dereniowski, better known online as MD Motivator, initially met Jaylen Brown at an event in Boston and asked if he wanted to give away a car to a family or some people. Brown agreed to that request.

Then Dereniowski met the woman and one of her children at Boston Common. What began as a simple interaction eventually turned into an emotional surprise, which neither the mother nor child could have expected.

The pair initially came to Dereniowski wanting a picture before he started talking to them and learned more about their family.

During the conversation, the woman revealed she was raising four children—three boys and a girl—as a single mother. She also explained the family did not have a car, which became an obvious challenge for a household of five.

Dereniowski then offered the child an opportunity to get his shoes signed by Jaylen Brown, and that was when the surprise became even more personal.

After meeting the family, Brown recognized the mother from her work at a Boys and Girls Club and acknowledged the positive work she had done in the community.

Instead of just signing the shoes and sending the family on their way, Brown and Dereniowski had something bigger planned.

They blindfolded the mother and child and took them to a brand-new 2027 Nissan Sentra and revealed that the vehicle belonged to them, and their emotional reaction was pretty immediate.

Both the mother and child began crying after realizing they had been given the car. The vehicle was provided with the involvement of Shane Sullivan of Sullivan Brothers Toyota, turning what was an ordinary encounter at Boston Common into a life-changing moment for the family.

For Brown, this gesture also carried some personal significance.

This video was most likely recorded before Jaylen Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers from the Boston Celtics, and it shows Brown's love for the city. Even after leaving Boston, his connection with the city is very clear.

Brown spent his first ten seasons of his NBA career with the Celtics after they selected him with the third overall pick in the 2016 NBA Draft. He became an NBA champion and Finals MVP before the Celtics eventually decided to trade him to the Sixers this offseason.

But this particular moment had nothing to do with basketball.

Dereniowski has built a massive online following just through these simple acts of kindness, often beginning videos with just simple conversations or requests and then surprising people with massive financial assistance or gifts, and this time Brown was there to help make the surprise even bigger.

A mother who arrived at Boston Common without a vehicle left with a brand-new one, and the fact that Brown had already recognized her community work made the emotional moment even more fitting.

title: The Vikings Snagged a Pair of Bruisers
description: A football roster is always in the process of being adjusted. However, the degree of roster change in late August […]
fullText:
A football roster is always in the process of being adjusted. However, the degree of roster change in late August and early September is particularly notable. Things are no different in Minnesota.

Yesterday, the Vikings snagged a pair of newcomers. Consider what the team's official social media had to say: "The #Vikings have signed TE Cam Grandy and DL Naquan Jones to the practice squad. TE Marshall Lang has been released from the practice squad."

Note that Minnesota went into these decisions with an open spot on the practice squad. As a result, going +2 with new players alongside just a -1 made the math work.

In Cam Grandy, the Vikings are welcoming a tight end who boasts good size. He's a sturdy 6'5″ and 253 pounds (but a spot like PFF lists him as being a touch larger, coming in at 260 on there). For comparison, T.J. Hockenson is listed as being 6'5″ and 248 pounds. Josh Oliver, meanwhile, is a hulking 6'5″ and 264 pounds.

A large part of the intrigue for the 26-year-old tight end is that he has demanded respect in the past for his blocking.

In 2024, Grandy earned a 74.9 pass blocking grade on PFF. He then upped the ante in 2025 with a 77.0 PFF grade. As a run blocker, the grades aren't quite so promising — 65.6 and then 61.0 — but there's promise here for the well-built TE.

Consider what SB Nation's Cincy Jungle had to say on the tight end: "As for Grandy, he's been a solid blocking tight end for several years now in Cincinnati. But with this being one of the deepest positions on the Bengals roster, Grandy knew he was better off finding another roster to work up the ranks with."

— 
— 
— 

And then there's the Naquan Jones add, who is a veteran nose tackle.

At least at the PFF level, Mr. Jones hasn't often been a difference maker. His outlier season arrived in 2024 when he posted a 63.2 grade while working with the Arizona Cardinals (as a teammate of Kyler Murray, for whatever that's worth). Jones tossed up a career-high 3 sacks that year, a nice total for a player who lines up directly across from the center.

Listed at 6'3″ and 313 pounds, Jones is a 28-year-old defender who first got into the NFL as an undrafted talent in 2021. He has since played for the Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals, Miami Dolphins, Los Angeles Chargers, and Houston Texans.

Now a Viking, Jones will begin by trying to get activated for the game-day roster before then demanding a full-time spot on the active roster.

Nolan Teasley isn't done yet. In the coming days, the GM will continue to consider his various options. Sometimes, that's going to be focused on working with the in-house talent to get an extension done. At other times, it's going to involve fielding trade calls, looking at who's available, and the various other parts of maintaining an NFL roster. We'll see if any other developments arise.

The Vikings' Week 1 game is going to take place on Sunday, September 13th when the Green Bay Packers come to U.S. Bank Stadium.

title: What Can Corey Kiner Bring to the Patriots As RB3?
description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel admitted to concerns about his team’s depth following their preseason finale. The Patriots relied heavily on backups throughout the preseason, hoping to build depth and uncover hidden contributors. After the run game struggled, Vrabel and his front office looked outside the building for running back depth. On August […] The post What Can Corey Kiner Bring to the Patriots As RB3? appeared first on The Lead.
fullText:
New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel admitted to concerns about his team's depth following their preseason finale.

The Patriots relied heavily on backups throughout the preseason, hoping to build depth and uncover hidden contributors. After the run game struggled, Vrabel and his front office looked outside the building for running back depth.

On August 29, the Patriots traded for Arizona Cardinals second-year running back Corey Kiner. With roster cutdowns complete, Kiner is one of three remaining running backs on New England's active roster.

Although Kiner's NFL experience is limited, the film shows promise as a physical back who can help keep the Patriots on schedule in 2026.

The Patriots are acquiring RB Corey Kiner in exchange for a ‘28 7th round pick, per @AdamSchefter.

A rookie UDFA last season, he totaled 12 carries for 58 yards and 2 catches for 15 yards across 4 games in ‘25. Had 204 carries for 1,153 yards and 4 TDs at Cincinnati in ‘24. pic.twitter.com/9UZovvIWmw

— Jack Aylmer (@Jack_Aylmer) August 29, 2026

Kiner entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025, spending training camp with the San Francisco 49ers before joining the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad. He didn't reach the Cardinals' active roster until December, when injuries opened an opportunity in Arizona's backfield.

Kiner appeared in four games for the Cardinals, logging 12 carries for 58 yards. The production was modest, but efficient, and his contact balance stood out most.

His Week 16 performance against the Atlanta Falcons best showed his ability to absorb contact. His nine-yard carry in the second quarter saw him truck star safety Jessie Bates, spin over a tackle attempt from All-Rookie selection Xavier Watts, and keep his balance before a third defender ultimately brought him down.

It was an early example of how it often takes multiple defenders to take him to the ground.

Kiner is officially listed at 5-foot-9, 209 pounds. His compact frame is a weapon in his bruising style, helping him get lower than defenders and deliver force. Pro Football Focus credited him with four missed tackles forced last season in just 12 carries. After finishing his senior season at Cincinnati with 82 missed tackles forced, that showed his defining skill translates to the next level.

Kiner's power continued to flash in the 2026 preseason, where he tallied 39 carries for 180 yards and two touchdowns. As he continues to adjust to NFL competition, his quick, purposeful footwork stands out. When he approaches the line of scrimmage, he takes short, quick steps that keep his options for cutback lanes open. Paired with good patience, he has built a film package of a promising between-the-tackles runner.

#Patriots HC Mike Vrabel on newly-acquired RB Corey Kiner:

“I like that group… Corey was somebody that we liked last year. We wanted to try to acquire [him] last year, and he went somewhere else. He had a really good preseason, so we just felt like that was a good addition to… pic.twitter.com/l3HXjDkYeI

— Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) August 31, 2026

One of the few positions where the Patriots had a surplus of talent was wide receiver. So, in the days after Vrabel's comments about the lack of depth, New England traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety and special teams contributor Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick.

Less than a week later, the Patriots flipped the pick acquired from Houston to the Cardinals for Kiner. In other words, New England turned its surplus at wide receiver into depth at safety, special teams and running back.

For Kiner specifically, it was a sign that the Patriots saw enough in his limited body of work to go outside the organization rather than settle for their existing RB3 options.

The Patriots tried out several running backs during preseason: Jam Miller, Hassan Haskins, JaMycal Hasty, and Lan Larison. The entire unit struggled, totaling just 259 yards on 79 carries, under 3.3 yards per carry.

Comparing the raw efficiency numbers between New England's backs and Kiner is not perfect. Kiner ran behind a different offensive line in a different system and faced different competition. Still, his combination of power, footwork, and patience was apparent regardless of the play result.

As of September 1, Haskins and Larison have signed with the Patriots' practice squad. Although largely ineffective in preseason, both showed New England enough to warrant a longer look. Haskins, who has been around the NFL for the past four years, brings kickoff return experience. Larison's upside as a receiving back took a hit with a pair of drops in the preseason finale, but that role largely remains vacant on the Patriots.

If anything, New England's decision to keep Haskins and Larison on the practice squad while also adding Kiner makes the running back room even deeper than previously anticipated.

Opportunities behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson may be scarce this season. However, if the Patriots need someone to step into an early-down role, Kiner's physical running style gives them a back capable of finding yards in tight spaces, absorbing contact and keeping the offense moving forward.

title: Dodgers predicted to make smart final decision on Shohei Ohtani's pitching rehab
description: This would be a smart choice from the Dodgers.
fullText:
Dodgers predicted to make smart final decision on Shohei Ohtani's pitching rehab originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The last time Shohei Ohtani was on the mound for the Los Angeles Dodgers was July 3.

At the time, Ohtani was a borderline National League Cy Young Award candidate.

Since then, the two-way superstar has been dealing with lingering left knee inflammation and right biceps discomfort.

Those injuries have kept Ohtani away from the rubber, but he continues to rehab and do throwing progressions.

If Ohtani's pitching rehab is affecting his hitting, should the Dodgers end his attempt at a return to the mound?

Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller says yes.

"Unless they can somehow definitively rule that out, Dave Roberts and the Dodgers' high-level decision-makers need to start asking themselves if it's really worth it to continue with his pitching rehab," Miller wrote after Ohtani had a .795 OPS in August, his worst OPS in a calendar month since April 2022.

A .795 OPS is a solid month for the average hitter, but this is Ohtani we are talking about. At this point, the Dodgers expect him to be at a .900 OPS or higher in a given month.

MORE:Cubs trade deadline addition Clay Holmes likely to opt out of $12M 2027 player option

Does Los Angeles really need Ohtani to pitch anyway? Probably not.

"After all, they already have (provided they stay healthy) a dynamite starting rotation for the postseason featuring Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, each with a sub-2.85 ERA for the year," Miller added.

For Ohtani's health and the impact he can have at the plate, the Dodgers should consider shutting him down from pitching for the year.

title: Gautam Gambhir, Aaqib Javed part of same management team:  Iceland Cricket creates hilarious 'international management personnel of nightmares'
description: With the recent management decisions making a mockery of Pakistani cricket, Iceland Cricket has now dragged Gautam Gambhir into the fray.
fullText:
Iceland Cricket published a viral "management personnel of nightmares" poking fun at recent off-field controversies across world cricket.

The mock team features India's Gautam Gambhir as head coach, Pakistan's Aaqib Javed as head of selectors, and Imam-ul-Haq as team physio.

Rob Key and Harry Brook were targeted over England's relaxed, golf-heavy team culture and off-field banter.

Iceland Cricket's social media account, long the sport's most reliable satirical mirror, has delivered another sharp critique of international cricket's current administrative absurdities.

In a post that quickly went viral across the cricket community, the handle assembled a mock "international management personnel of nightmares."

The satirical list takes aim at the ongoing chaos spanning several major boards. From Gautam Gambhir's intense coaching persona in India and Aaqib Javed's volatile selection policies in Pakistan to England's leisure-heavy "Bazball" team culture, it takes a dig at everyone.

The mock setup weaves together current figures whose recent public controversies, tactical friction, or off-field reputations make them a uniquely disastrous combination on paper.

MORE: Former Pakistan selector claims Babar Azam 'protected' Imam-ul-Haq in faking injury

At the top of this fictional chain of command sits Gautam Gambhir as head coach, operating alongside Aaqib Javed as head of selectors. The joke lands because of the sheer operational paradox it presents. Combining Gambhir's uncompromising, high-pressure persona with Aaqib's recent habit of purging senior players mid-series is a recipe for instant combustion.

We can create a current international management personnel of nightmares:

Head coach: Gautam Gambhir
Head of selectors: Aqib Javed
Captain and post-match party organiser: Harry Brook
Director of golf: Rob Key
Physio: Imam-ul-Haq

In reality, marrying Gambhir's demand for militant discipline with Aaqib's erratic selection resets would guarantee a total dressing-room mutiny before the tea break on day one. The lower half of the management structure is equally pointed.

Assigning Imam-ul-Haq the role of "Team Physio" is a direct, brutal nod to the ongoing fallout from the Lord's Test. With the opener's calf strain conveniently coinciding with Pakistan's second-innings collapse, handing Imam the medical kit is satire operating at its sharpest.

Meanwhile, England's laid-back, vibecentric ethos gets its own designated department. Naming Rob Key as "Director of Golf" and Harry Brook as "Captain and post-match party organiser" perfectly mocks the leisure-heavy culture defining the Bazball era.

MORE: 'Can't say he faked it, but…': PCB director Aaqib Javed wants inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq's injury at Lord's

The humour in Iceland Cricket's tweet relies entirely on raw accuracy. Assigning Imam-ul-Haq the role of "Team Physio" is a direct nod to the recent controversy at Lord's, where the opener's calf strain coincided with a second-innings collapse and subsequent allegations from former selectors regarding manipulated fitness reports.

Similarly, pairing Gambhir's uncompromising, high-pressure coaching environment with Aaqib Javed's erratic selection policy creates an operational paradox.

In real life, combining Gambhir's demand for rigid intensity with Aaqib's habit of purging senior players mid-series would guarantee total dressing-room collapse within a week.

For England, naming Rob Key as "Director of Golf" and Harry Brook as "Post-Match Party Organiser" mocks the laid-back, vibecentric ethos that has defined the team's leadership. While effective during winning stretches, that casual posture routinely draws public cynicism the moment results slip on away tours.

There is, however, a grim reality buried in the humor. Until major boards can display a modicum of operational stability and sound decision-making, supporters will continue to find more clarity in a joke tweet from Reykjavik than in the official communications coming out of Lahore, London, or Mumbai.

title: Woods gets five-year driving ban after plea agreement over car crash
description: Tiger Woods has been banned from driving for five years and hit with a fine after entering a plea agreement for reckless driving following a car crash in Florida in March. The 15-time major winner was arrested and spent eight hours in jail before being bailed after his Land Rover rolled over in a collision with a pick-up truck towing a trailer.
fullText:
Tiger Woods has been banned from driving for five years and hit with a fine after entering a plea agreement for reckless driving following a car crash in Florida in March.

The 15-time major winner was arrested and spent eight hours in jail before being bailed after his Land Rover rolled over in a collision with a pick-up truck towing a trailer.

He had previously entered a written plea of not guilty via his lawyers to charges of driving under the influence, property damage and a refusal to submit to testing.

Appearing at Martin County Courthouse on Wednesday morning, he agreed to the lesser charge, with Judge Darren Steele ordering Woods' driving licence be suspended for five years alongside a fine of $1,000. An additional careless driving citation also carries a five-year suspension, but the judge allowed that to run concurrently.

Woods walked away unhurt from the crash, escaping out of his passenger door, and, while he passed a breathalyser test for alcohol, the 50-year-old refused to submit to a urinary test for drugs. That refusal earned him an additional $500.

According to the initial police affidavit, Woods was observed by the investigating officers to be "sweating profusely" while acting "lethargic and slow" with eyes that were "bloodshot and glassy".

He admitted he "was looking down at his cell phone and changing the radio station" in the moments before the crash and "did not notice the vehicle in front of him had slowed down".

Woods told the authorities he had not consumed any alcohol but admitted to taking "a few" prescription medications and had done so earlier in the morning while insisting he had not had any illegal drugs.

Multiple sobriety exercises were conducted, where he struggled to follow instructions, leading a deputy to conclude: "How he performed on the exercises and based on my training, knowledge and experience, I believe Woods' normal faculties were impaired and he was unable to safely operate the motor vehicle."

Woods underwent emergency surgery after suffering multiple leg injuries following a serious car accident in California in February 2021. He has not competed on the PGA Tour since July 2024.

The affidavit stated Woods said he had 20 surgeries on his leg as a result of that crash, plus seven operations on his back, while the report also noted Woods was "limping and stumbling."

Woods later wrote on X: "I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in.

"I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritize my wellbeing and work toward lasting recovery."

Woods was also arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) offences in 2017 after being found asleep at the wheel of his car in Jupiter, Florida.

He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving after it emerged he had had five prescription drugs in his system at the time.

In 2009, he crashed his car into a fire hydrant and tree outside his home in an incident that led to a spectacular unravelling of his private life.

title: Hadjar to miss Italian Grand Prix with injury as Liam Lawson deputizes
description: Isack Hadjar’s ongoing wrist injury has ruled him out of this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix where his Red Bull will again be driven by Liam Lawson. The Frenchman, in his debut season with the team, sustained the problem during the summer break and missed the first race back in Zandvoort a fortnight ago.
fullText:
Isack Hadjar's ongoing wrist injury has ruled him out of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix where his Red Bull will again be driven by Liam Lawson.

The Frenchman, in his debut season with the team, sustained the problem during the summer break and missed the first race back in Zandvoort a fortnight ago.

Lawson – who was unceremoniously dumped by Red Bull after just two races last year – finished seventh on his return to the team from Racing Bulls.

A Red Bull statement read: "Liam Lawson will drive alongside Max Verstappen at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break.

"The team is closely monitoring his rehabilitation and will take no unnecessary risks with his return to competition and wishes him a speedy recovery."

Yuki Tsunoda, who was left without a drive for this year following his Red Bull exit at the end of last season, will again sit in for Lawson in the Racing Bull car having finished 11th on his return at Zandvoort.

title: Patriots get bad news on Christian Gonzalez contract extension talks
description: This update on Christian Gonzalez's talks with the Patriots is not a good one.
fullText:
Patriots get bad news on Christian Gonzalez contract extension talks originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New England Patriots and superstar cornerback Christian Gonzalez are in the middle of contract extension talks, which would likely have to make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

But after Devon Witherspoon of the Seattle Seahawks signed a massive $132 million, four-year contract, things have hit an impasse between Gonzalez and the Patriots.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the latest update is a bit concerning, as the two sides are still far apart on a deal, and there are reportedly multiple elements of an extension that they are not close to agreeing upon.

"My understanding of this situation is that if Gonzalez were to sign a market-setting deal -- and it will need to be just that -- then it has to be buttoned up. And the sides are not close on several elements of the deal."

Gonzalez might've been the best player on the field for the Patriots in their Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, and an extension makes a lot of sense. Good cornerbacks are not easy to come by.

But spending so much money on Gonzalez, which would need to break the $132 million mark set by Witherspoon this offseason, is something the Patriots seemingly aren't too inclined to do.

That could be the case, or Gonzalez could be asking for a significant raise from Witherspoon's figure, further complicating a deal.

MORE: Why Patriots traded Kayshon Boutte to Texans for Jaylen Reed and a 7th-round draft pick

The 24-year-old superstar is worth a massive new deal, but the Patriots might be saving some of their money to spend on Drake Maye when he'll need an extension, which could be agreed to as early as next offseason.

Gonzalez should be a core player the Patriots lock up, and there is mutual interest in a deal. The issue is, however, that the two sides are still far apart on an extension.

There is some real fear that a deal won't be agreed upon, which would be a massive mistake for the Patriots. Unfortunately, the Gonzalez contract situation is one to closely monitor, as the Patriots might be forced into a corner with what to do with him long-term.

It might be too soon to totally panic, but Patriots fans should be a little bit worried about how these extension talks have gone thus far.

title: Carse omitted from England squad for third Test
description: England leave Brydon Carse out of their squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.
fullText:
England have omitted Brydon Carse from their squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

The Durham seamer was dropped for the second Test at Lord's after he was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub on 22 August.

The 31-year-old remains under investigation by Derbyshire police, who say they are looking into allegations of assault.

Carse's replacement, 23-year-old Sonny Baker, has retained his place in England's 15-man party.

Surrey's Matthew Fisher has been dropped from an otherwise unchanged England squad as they seek to complete a series clean-sweep over Pakistan.

The third Test in Birmingham starts on Wednesday, 9 September at 11:00 BST.

With six white-ball matches against Sri Lanka to follow the Test series, England may consider resting seamers Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, all of whom feature in the limited-overs set-up.

While the trio have been named in the Test squad, they may be rotated in favour of Baker, Essex pace bowler Sam Cook and Derbyshire spinner Shoaib Bashir.

Cook, 29, played his one Test against Zimbabwe last summer while 22-year-old Bashir is yet to feature in this series, with England preferring an all-pace attack.

Baker made his only Test appearance to date in a much-changed line-up against New Zealand at The Oval in June.

Carse remains available for selection for Durham and finished with match figures of 4-95 in their win over Gloucestershire last week.

However, he has not been picked in the XI for their match against Northamptonshire, which started on Wednesday.

Pakistan made the extraordinary move of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach prior to the Edgbaston Test.

Sarfaraz Ahmed has replaced by Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson, while Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad, all of whom have featured in the series, are among the players dropped.

England beat Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs in the first Test at Headingley and sealed series victory with a win by 194 runs at Lord's last week.

title: Nationals’ rookie duo makes MLB history Tuesday night
description: The future is bright in Washington.
fullText:
The Washington Nationals made MLB history Tuesday night, as rookie teammates Jared Simpson and Yohandy Morales accomplished something no duo had done since 1900.

MORE: Top MLB prospect, 20-year-old catching phenom called up late Monday night

Sep 1, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Nationals pitcher Jared Simpson (72) throws to the Atlanta Braves during the seventh inning at Nationals Park. Mandatory Credit: Brad Mills-Imagn Images

In their respective MLB debuts, Morales and Simpson delivered performances that immediately put their names in the record books. Morales went 3-for-5 at the plate, launched a home run and finished just a triple short of hitting for the cycle. Simpson, meanwhile, tossed three scoreless innings and earned the win as Washington defeated the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves 9-5.

The Nationals called up both players before Tuesday's game as MLB rosters expanded to 28 players. Their immediate impact helped Washington secure an impressive victory against a division contender.

Morales, a 24-year-old infielder, was selected by Washington in the second round of the 2023 MLB Draft out of the University of Miami. Since being drafted, he has established himself as one of the organization's top offensive prospects. He ranks second in the Nationals' minor league system in RBI with 220 and doubles with 79, while ranking third in hits with 385 and fourth in home runs with 47.

MORE: Red Sox get their stars back & it's still not enough

Simpson, a 26-year-old left-handed pitcher, has also enjoyed a strong minor league career. He posted a 2.30 ERA and recorded 73 strikeouts over 58.2 innings between Double-A Harrisburg and Triple-A Rochester this season. Since Washington selected him in the eighth round out of the University of Iowa in 2023, Simpson has recorded 137 strikeouts, the most among left-handed pitchers in the Nationals' minor league system.

The performances from Morales and Simpson came at an important point in Washington's season. With 21 games remaining, the Nationals entered Wednesday seven games behind the Braves in the division and seven games out of a National League Wild Card spot.

While Washington faces a difficult path toward the postseason, the historic debuts provided an encouraging glimpse at the organization's future. Morales' power and offensive production, combined with Simpson's ability to miss bats and limit scoring, could make the rookie duo an important part of the Nationals' plans moving forward.

title: Peoria Rivermen add a winger from Ukraine, and another who went viral for a big hit
description: The Peoria Rivermen added a pair of wings for the 2026-27 SPHL season, one from Ukraine, the other known for an open-ice hit that went viral.
fullText:
PEORIA — The Peoria Rivermen added to their roster on Wednesday when they reached agreement with a pair of wingers, one from Chicago and one a native of Ukraine.

Peoria signed right wing Alfred Rotiroti and left wing Bohdan Zinchenko, both of whom played in the low-A FPHL last season.

Rotiroti produced a viral video on TikTok as a college player at Rivier University, where his open-ice hit on a Keene State player sent the opponent airborne and somersaulted him onto the ice.

The 5-foot-11, 187-pound scrappy forward also fought renowned Quad City Storm enforcer Divyne Apollon last season in his rookie year as a pro.

Rotiroti played four years of NCAA Div.-III college hockey with Rivier, serving as captain in his final season.

His college career included 15 goals and 14 assists in 93 games. He turned pro last spring with Biloxi in the FPHL, notching four goals with three assists in 16 games, while adding 39 penalty minutes.

Zinchenko, meanwhile, is a Kyiv, Ukraine native and veteran of three pro seasons.

He has played 120 regular-season games in the FPHL over the last three seasons with Danbury, Danville, Athens and Indiana.

The 6-foot, 195-pound 24-year-old is a Concordia University grad who was owner and head coach of a hockey team venture in Montreal known as BZ Hockey Club.

The Rivermen have 13 players under contract now for the 2026-27 SPHL season.

Defense: Tyler Ryder, Kylar Fenton, Gunner Moore.

Forwards: Alec Baer, Cayden Cahill, Cooper Board, Will Redick, Braydon Barker, T.J. Koufis, Michael McChesney.

Dave Eminian is the Journal Star sports editor. He has covered the Rivermen for 42 seasons. Reach him at deminian@pjstar.com or on X @icetimecleve.

title: Late-night transfer fallout sparks Chelsea-Monaco row
description: How Chelsea, Everton and Monaco all missed out after late-night drama on deadline day. Nizaar Kinsella reports.
fullText:
One source with connections to both Chelsea and Monaco said the clubs had "played with fire and got burned".

Indeed, the late-night transfer drama that involved Folarin Balogun, Everton, Monaco, Lamine Camara and Chelsea saw all parties lose out.

Camara - a 22-year-old Senegalese international midfielder - had been a target for Chelsea as they prepared for the £125m sale of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City.

But Monaco were adamant he was going nowhere for the fee Chelsea were willing to pay.

"I've been speaking to them for the last 10 days," said Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said.

"At around 16:00 BST yesterday we got contact from Chelsea. The answer was the same: no."

Instead, the Ligue 1 club had allowed United States international striker Balogun, 25, to fly to Merseyside to complete a £40m move to Everton. According to Monaco, Camara had agreed to stay with the club.

With three hours remaining of the transfer window, Chelsea were content with their midfield options, despite the sale of Fernandez, after failing with enquiries for Camara and Roma's Manu Kone.

But issues with Balogun's Everton medical presented an opportunity for Chelsea.

"Of course, Chelsea saw an opportunity," Scuro added.

"'Monaco need money, Balogun is struggling there, let's go and try.' Chelsea called us and said: 'Maybe we can be the solution.'

"At that moment, we had to open the door to discussions."

Negotiations were back underway with Monaco at 20:00 BST and a £47m fee was agreed shortly after.

Meanwhile, Everton failed to find alternatives to Balogun and revived their move with minutes before the deadline.

Chelsea had completed all the necessary paperwork for Camara and did not need to submit a deal sheet - a request to the Premier League for additional time to complete a transfer, post the deadline.

But the plug was pulled. Monaco acknowledge Camara was disappointed after he had spoken to manager Xabi Alonso, passed a medical and signed a contract until 2033.

"What happened was that around 22:00 BST our time, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised there was no issue and decided they were ready to sign the contract [for Balogun]," Scuro told reporters on Wednesday afternoon.

"As soon as we received that information, we came back to Chelsea and said there was no deal. Because that's also fair. It's part of the game."

Chelsea were left furious, claiming Monaco informed them in writing that the deal would not proceed rather than communicating the decision by phone.

Monaco thought - by signing a deal sheet, five minutes before the 23:00 BST deadline, to allow Everton extra time to complete the transfer of Balogun - they had secured the sale they needed to help comply with Uefa's financial regulations.

The Ligue 1 side were under pressure to generate 150m euros in player sales this summer, and had raised 106m euros from departures.

Another twist was still to come.

In the early hours of Tuesday morning, the former Arsenal striker had a change of heart which saw him leave Everton's Finch Farm training ground without signing for the club.

Scuro claims Balogun felt he was mistreated while at Everton's training ground, something the Premier League club disputes.

"We had to respect his decision," Scuro added.

"We found solutions, challenged the medical assessment and worked through the issues.

"I don't want to create a war with Chelsea or Everton.

"My role is to protect Monaco and act in the club's best interests. That's what I've done since I arrived.

"It's not about being loved by people outside the club. It's about doing what Monaco needs."

Scuro says it is possible Monaco will look at selling other players to countries whose transfer window remains open in order to acquire the funds they need.

The Monaco chief is open to welcoming back both players. Camara has already returned to training and is set to feature in their upcoming match away at Paris St-Germain on Friday night.

"I really understand because a player can get excited by conversations with a coach and by everything a club like Chelsea can offer," Scuro continued.

"This is not the end of the world. It's one opportunity. For a player with his level of talent, I'm very confident he will soon have even better options and offers than the one he had yesterday."

According to sources close to Camara, Liverpool also retain a long-standing interest in a future deal.

Chelsea had been considering Camara as an option to replace Fernandez for the final 10 days of the window.

Of course, the Londoners could have forced a deal through sooner but it might have meant overpaying because, as sources had previously explained, Monaco saw Camara as not for sale throughout the majority of the window - barring those few hours on Tuesday evening - but for "exceptional" offers.

Chelsea were blindsided by the collapse of the deal and there was little they could have done to revive it or sign an alternative before the deadline.

They did, however, have the option of cancelling Fernandez's move to Manchester City but opted not to do so out of a sense of "professionalism".

Chelsea wanted a midfielder to replace Fernandez but there was never any desperation as the club only wanted to do so on its own terms.

Alonso sees captain Reece James primarily as a midfield option, alongside Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and new signings Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco within his 27-man squad.

Yet injuries to Caicedo and Henderson, coupled with James' workload, meant full-back Malo Gusto was used in midfield during the 4-3 victory over Brighton, a match in which Chelsea recorded 25.6% possession, their lowest figure since records began in 2003-04.

Alonso could have selected Barco, 21, who came on as a second-half substitute, but the club want to carefully manage the signing from Strasbourg as he returns to the Premier League after a short-lived spell at Brighton.

There remains debate over whether Chelsea have sufficient depth and quality in midfield, with the club retaining the option of revisiting a move for Camara or another midfielder in January.

They could also look to strengthen other positions having been left delighted at making a net profit in the transfer market while adding quality.

Chelsea signed World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez, France international Maxence Lacroix and club-record £117m signing Morgan Rogers, as well as experienced striker Danny Welbeck and full-backs Pep Chavarria and Marco Palestra.

It's now on the manager and squad they have built to attempt to match Chelsea's ambitions on the pitch, starting with Sunday's trip to champions Arsenal.

title: Dana White's Contender Series 90: Grading the winners
description: MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom grades the DWCS 90 contract winners and breaks down their potential for success in the UFC.
fullText:
Week 4 of Dana White's Contender Series (2026) took place on Tuesday in Las Vegas, and we're grading the winners from the five-fight card, which streamed on ESPN+ from the UFC Apex. With a simple but digestible format that has had the MMA fanbase responding, this series has shown to have legs in multiple ways while serving as a crockpot for contenders the UFC matchmakers can use to fill their roster for future events. With that trend in mind, I once again will be taking a look at the winning fighters, regardless of whether or not they won a UFC contract, and grading their performances in regard to their probability of returning to a UFC stage.

Result: Adam Livingston def. Hunter Smith via split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)

Despite getting the desired win and UFC contract, I found it difficult to give Adam Livingston's spirited effort anything more than a solid B from a grading perspective.

Although I believe the judges ultimately got it right, I couldn't help but shake the feeling that Hunter Smith was constantly on the brink of taking over the proverbial steering wheel in this fight. In fact, I found myself feeling for the frustrations of Smith's corner regarding his incorrect circling and lack of follow-ups when in positive positions.

Both Livingston and Smith started with the right ideas and shot selection to begin the fight, but each combatant ended up straying from their effective tactics in favor of headhunting. Livingston, in particular, looked really good when jabbing and working the body (as Smith was clearly favoring his right side by the end of the contest).

Hopefully, we see more of Livingston's fundamentals and a tad less spinning stuff from the native New Yorker next time out. If it is an international booking, then book Livingston in a potential barnburner opposite someone like Damian Rzepecki.

Result: Gabriel Lorenco def. Charlie Cleveland via knockout (punches) – Round 1, 2:02

Although it didn't last long, Gabriel Lorenco earns the obligatory A that this show's standards have set for fast finishers that understand the assignment.

Lorenco's opponent, Charlie Cleveland, came out with some solid looks from his classic southpaw stance. Unfortunately for Cleveland, Lorenco's length and power made up for the rawness that still needs to be cooked out of his game.

But with Lorenco securing yet another quick finish, I suppose the Brazilian will have to continue to learn on what will be a much bigger stage. I believe that Anthony Wint would be a solid and sensible matchup for Lorenco, but the UFC matchmakers will likely feed the American footballer a couple more gimmies before any real tests.

Even if Lorenco is not worthy of the same promotional hype as Wint, I suspect that he, too, gets the Terrance Chapman treatment coming off this show

Result: Silvestre Sanchez def. Liam McCracken via TKO (punches) – Round 3, 2:44

In what was easily the best fight and prospect of the night, Silvestre Sanchez earns an emphatic A for his third-round finish over a tough Liam McCracken.

Sanchez, who looked a weight class larger than McCracken with his pre-USADA shoulders, got to show off a lot of his skills in this fight. From solid takedowns and grappling along the fence to his combinations on the feet, Sanchez's pressure seems to be a hallmark of his style.

I can be critical of this show's propensity to push products too quickly to the mass markets, but Sanchez is definetley someone the matchmakers can plug-and-play in what has traditionally been their deepest division.

I know prospect showdowns can be risky, but I believe that Sanchez vs. Stan Dorsainvil has Fight of the Year potential written all over it should the UFC brass want to put that together.

Result: Modestino Rodrigues def. Brandon Holmes via TKO (punches) – Round 1, 0:15

Although we barely even got to see a fight, I, once again, feel compelled to give out the obligatory A that the bar of this show has set for fast finishers like Modestino Rodrigues.

I sympathize with Brandon Holmes given the early nature of Chris Tagnoni's stoppage (which was a classic case of referee over-correction due to his late stoppage in the Charlie Cleveland fight), but Rodrigues deserves his due for doing his job as a slight underdog.

Luckily for Rodrigues, middleweights and above who win on this show are often rewarded with main-card gimmies on Fight Nights, while entertaining lighter-weight class fighters like Nathaniel Wood can't get favorable matchups or featured slots to save their lives. But I digress.

Expect Mick Maynard to force-feed us Rodrigues in a prominent Fight Night spot soon, likely against anyone ranging from Julien Leblanc to Donte Johnson.

Result: Adam Darby def. Patrick Rivera via TKO (doctor stoppage) – Round 3, 2:45

Despite technically getting a stoppage win, I had a hard time giving Adam Darby anything higher than a B for his part in what ultimately ended up being a one-sided beatdown that was more depressing than it was entertaining.

Unfortunately for Patrick Rivera, whatever plan he and his team came into this fight with appeared completely futile by the end of the first frame. And whether you want to point to the deceptive nature of Darby's 'death by a thousand papercuts' style or MMA's cold and apathetic corner culture when it comes to coaches and corners failing to protect their own fighters, watching Rivera's corner miss all the non-verbals that were given is something that I have a harder and harder time watching as I age with this sport.

Kerry Hatley, who has made a marked improvement from his "Kumite Kerry" reputation for allowing near-deaths to precipitate stoppages, ended up making the right call for both Rivera's brain health and for the sake of the audience who had to watch him senselessly waste it at the behest of his corner.

Nevertheless, Darby ultimately makes an interesting addition to the UFC's welterweight stable, and I apologize if it seems that I'm letting the other moving pieces in the main event overshadow Darby's disciplined performance. Expect Darby to be booked on the next English or European show, likely opposite an action-fighting Brazilian like Jose Henrique Souza.

title: Remember these clips if the Dallas Cowboys stink
description: It's once again that time of year when Cowboys hype rockets out of control.
fullText:
It's a day that ends in "y" so that means the Dallas Cowboys are all over the sports talk shows. Brian Schottenheimer's side will be featured on Sunday Night Football for a Week 1 matchup against the hated New York Giants and we'll finally have some meaningful football to fuel reactions. But until things kick off, the only thing to do is to look ahead and make bold claims.

Both Jordan Rodgers and Adam Schefter took advantage of the opportunity on Wednesday's Get Up.

"On paper, this defense can get them to the Super Bowl because of how good the offense is," Rodgers surmised. "This defense needs to go from one of the worst to just good, middle of the pack."

Schefter agreed, channeling his rosy outlook for the Cowboys into the most important thing—how it impacts Stephen A. Smith.

"I got some bad news for Stephen A. Smith," Schefter said. "The Dallas Cowboys are coming!"

It feels like an annual tradition to hype up the Cowboys before they inevitably have a disappointing season. We've been doing it for three decades now with precious little evidence showing that it ever works.

No doubt, some of you want it to stop. Considering the team's accomplishments in comparison to some other franchises this century, there is absolutely no reason for them to dominate as much of the spotlight as they do. Yet I am going to offer a bit of a rebuttal steeped in cynicism.

The America's Team thing worked. There's a reason why Dallas finds itself in the A or B block even when they don't warranted it. Heck, even when there's nothing of substance to really discuss. It's not that they have to shove the Cowboys down our throats all the time but they also have to do what's best to stand out in an attention economy.

MORE: Previewing all 16 NFC teams & predicting every record in 2026

People who are tired by the song and dance can take solace in knowing that there are always a blessing of wonderful clips that don't age well whenever the Cowboys fall on their face. So if history is any guide, a little patience is required for a snarky payout down the line.

Or, if you are a believer in Dallas, bookmark this page and dance all over my grave if the Cowboys do, in fact, win it all.

title: Aubameyang ‘humiliated’ as ex-Arsenal striker quits Gabon national team
description: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang cites 2025 Africa Cup of Nations treatment as captain steps away from Gabon duty.
fullText:
Gabon captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has announced that he is stepping back from the national team, saying he felt "humiliated" by his exclusion and subsequent reinstatement after the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in Morocco.

The top scorer in the history of the Panthers was singled out by the Gabonese government as responsible for the AFCON failure.

"They humiliated and smeared me even though I played at the AFCON while injured," the 37-year-old said in a television interview.

"This is the last straw, and I'd rather stop here."

Gabon were eliminated from the AFCON in the group stage after three defeats, the last of which came against Ivory Coast.

"It's a part of our national identity that has been weakened," Gabonese President Brice Oligui Nguema said at the time.

The government fired the coaching staff, suspended the team until further notice and sidelined Aubameyang and 38-year-old Bruno Ecuele Manga.

The suspension of these veteran mainstays of the squad sparked a wave of outrage among Gabonese supporters.

"I think the team's problems run much deeper than the little person that I am," said Aubameyang, who was one of Europe's top strikers during his time at Borussia Dortmund and Arsenal.

The Gabonese striker has set himself what is likely to be a final challenge in Europe, leaving Marseille to join Deportivo La Coruna, who have just returned to La Liga after a long spell in the wilderness.

Gabon's new national team coach, Sebastien Migne, will now have to plan without Aubameyang as he prepares his team for their first qualifiers later this month for next year's AFCON.

Gabon are in Group A with World Cup quarter-finalists Morocco as well as Niger and Lesotho.

title: Notre Dame reveals tribute to Lou Holtz for 2026 season
description: A helmet honor connects the current roster to the last coach who delivered a Notre Dame national title.
fullText:
Notre Dame players will run onto the field this fall wearing a piece of college football history on their helmets. The school announced a decal honoring former head coach Lou Holtz for the 2026 season, six months after his death.

The decal shows "LOU" in white letters on a black background. Two hands forming an "L" shape flank the name. It will sit on the back lower right of the gold helmet.

Holtz died on March 4 at age 89 in Orlando, Florida. He is buried on the Notre Dame campus next to his wife, Beth.

MORE: 6 prediction market picks for College Football's Week 1

The legendary Notre Dame head coach Lou Holtz led the Fighting Irish from 1986 to 1996.

Notre Dame hired Holtz in 1986. He had already coached at William & Mary, North Carolina State, Arkansas and Minnesota, plus a stint with the NFL's New York Jets. His first two seasons in South Bend were rocky. The Irish went 5-6 in 1986 and 8-4 in 1987.

The turnaround came fast after those first two years. Notre Dame finished 12-0 in 1988 and beat West Virginia in the Fiesta Bowl. That season delivered the program's first national title in 11 years. It also included the famous "Catholics vs. Convicts" game, where Notre Dame snapped Miami's 36-game regular-season winning streak.

The Irish nearly repeated as champs in 1989. They went 12-1 and beat Colorado in the Orange Bowl. Their only loss came against Miami, which went on to win the national title that year.

Holtz coached 11 seasons at Notre Dame. He finished 100-30-2, with five bowl wins and four top-five finishes. He left after the 1996 season and later coached South Carolina from 1999 to 2004.

MORE: Kirk Herbstreit makes 2027 College Football Playoff National Championship pick

This is not the first time Notre Dame has used a helmet decal to honor a coach. The program did the same for Ara Parseghian in 2017. Parseghian died that August at age 94, and his decal read "ARA" in the spot normally reserved for "IRISH" above the facemask. Parseghian coached Notre Dame from 1964 to 1974 and won national titles in 1966 and 1973.

Notre Dame enters the 2026 college football season ranked fifth in the Coaches Poll and fourth in the AP Poll under head coach Marcus Freeman. The Irish are considered among the favorites to win a national title.

title: Monaco CEO breaks down Folarin Balogun's failed Everton deadline day transfer
description: AS Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro has gone into detail about U.S. Men's National Team striker Folarin Balogun's failed deadline day transfer to Premier League side Everton
fullText:
U.S. Men's National Team striker Folarin Balogun's prospective return to the Premier League is off after the 25-year-old former Arsenal academy star pulled out of a move to Everton at the last minute.

Tuesday at 11pm BST (5pm ET) marked the deadline in the English summer transfer window, and despite a last gasp effort to secure Balogun's signature by the Toffees, which would have netted AS Monaco some much-needed funds, the deal ultimately fell through in dramatic fashion.

Speaking with reporters on Wednesday after the dust had settled, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro gave a fascinating insight into exactly what went wrong on Tuesday between the clubs and Balogun, and what the future may hold for the World Cup star - who was at the center of one of the tournament's biggest controversies.

Admitting that the club's approach to the summer market was to raise funds in order to meet financial regulations, he commented, via Get The Football News France, "Clearly, we were open to discussing and finding a transfer for Balogun. He finished his third season. We had already worked in advance to replace him, and we were fully ready to do this. Things went very well with this strategy until we were almost there."

Since joining Monaco in 2023 from Arsenal, following loan stints with Middlesbrough and Reims, Balogun has found the back of the net 31 times in 91 games, providing a further 13 assists along the way in all competitions. Last season was particularly fruitful for the forward, scoring 19 goals in 43 appearances.

But with the club in need of funds and Balogun two years away from hitting free agency, Monaco clearly felt it was the right time to cash in, not naming him to any of their matchday squads so far this season and, ultimately, attempting to ship him off to Merseyside.

"During the day, we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton. Balogun flew yesterday morning to go for medicals and sign a contract," Scuro said. "Our plan worked very well in this moment in terms of revenue generation, squad planning, player transfers.

"Thilo [Kehrer] going (to Ajax), as announced, opened the space in the salary that we needed with the DNCG (French football's financial watchdog). Balogun, besides the salary, was also an important source of income for the club, which would help us also to balance the season."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

However, things began to unravel on Tuesday evening, as Scuro detailed. "Around 7 pm, we were contacted by Everton, raising questions about Balogun's medical, which, for our medical staff, as well as for the player's personal medical staff, made no sense at all," he said.

"The explanations were not enough to justify or to bring concerns regarding the future of the player, which there aren't. This discussion started between medical departments from here and there.

"It took Everton around 2-3 hours to go deep into the assessment and check with other doctors. This is a normal situation when the doctor of the club raises concerns. It's quite normal that clubs will look for other specialists, share the images and discuss the case. This was ongoing."

Around three hours passed by which point Everton gave the move the green light. However, in need of more time to finalize the deal, the teams triggered a Premier League rule allowing for an extension of an hour to complete a last-minute move.

"The Premier League has a mechanism in which you can request one extra hour to finish the paperwork. This was done," he said. "Five minutes to close the transfer window there, for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and 'Balo'. I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract.

"At the last moment, the players decided not to sign. And basically, Balogun's allegation is that I'm not feeling well because of the way the club treated me. I'm not feeling well because Everton's medical department raised doubts about my future or my health. I have nothing (no health problem), so I'm not comfortable signing a long contract here. And that's the way we finish our transfer window."

All the while, with Monaco in need of funds and Balogun failing his medical, Monaco agreed to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea, with the Blues on the lookout for a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, who moved to Manchester City for $169.1 million earlier that day.

But when Everton approved Balogun's medical, Monaco called off the sale of Camara - only then for the American to pull out of the move.

"So basically, the story about those two players and what happened yesterday was also new for me," Scuro noted. "It's the first time in my career that I saw a last day (deadline day) like this.

"It's not nice to stay the last two days of the transfer window until 3 a.m. in the office, trying to find solutions here and there. And this is something that we need to try to do better as a club, because it puts everyone in a situation where what is happening can happen. And it's not nice to be here, having to explain and having to face all the consequences of this.

• Manchester City turn down Manchester United's stunning deadline day inquiry

• Manchester City sign Everton's Iliman Ndiaye for $88 million after Cody Gakpo move fails

"And the reality is now that we are very, very happy that Lamine stayed. We want to be strong on the pitch. We want to grow this season, and we are going for that. And now we are still waiting for 'Balo' to come back for us to sit and discuss and to realize between us what's next.

"We still have other markets open, which we are having discussions about with different players, including 'Balo'. Let's see what can still happen until Thursday, because we still have markets that have the financial capacity to do something. And this is what happened, and this is where we are today."

title: Kroenke Inherits Uncertain Angels TV Network, Stadium Fight
description: The incoming owner is also inheriting the recently rebranded RSN.
fullText:
Stan Kroenke is inheriting a massive job to rebuild the Angels, on and off the field, as part of his landmark $4 billion deal to acquire the MLB club. A key part of that reconstruction is elevating Angels Broadcast Television (ABTV), the regional sports network that is part of the agreement.

Along with the team, Kroenke is acquiring ABTV from outgoing Angels owner Arte Moreno, with that television network very much in a transitional state. Soon after the Angels were one of nine MLB clubs to sever ties with the largely defunct Main Street Sports Group in early February, Moreno bought out the company's 50% interest in FanDuel Sports Network West, the RSN that the two entities previously shared.

Moreno and the Angels originally planned to retain the FanDuel name for the RSN, but rebranded to the ABTV moniker in May. Under the ABTV name, the network has been attempting to forge an uncertain path as cord-cutting and cord-nevering continue to batter much of the regional sports media business.

In part because of that, MLB commissioner Rob Manfred has increasingly pushed for a greater nationalization and pooling of the local media rights across the league. As part of ongoing labor negotiations with the MLB Players Association, management is also proposing to pool and split all local media rights evenly across the 30 teams—but in the context of a salary cap that the players fiercely oppose.

ABTV also airs the NHL's Kings, and has distribution deals with major Southern California distributors such as Spectrum, DirecTV, and Cox. Angels broadcasts are led by a popular on-air crew of Wayne Randazzo, Mark Gubicza, and Erica Weston. Kroenke is also acquiring KLAA-AM, the Angels' radio broadcaster, in the franchise deal. It will bear watching whether that platform's game announcers, Mark Langston and Terry Smith, will resume traveling to Angels road contests, as they haven't since the COVID-19 pandemic started.

Kroenke has shown to be a tough negotiator elsewhere in his sports empire when it comes to local broadcasting. His Altitude Sports & Entertainment, which airs the NBA's Nuggets and NHL's Avalanche that he also owns, had a contract dispute with Comcast that kept the network off of that carrier for five and a half years until reaching a new deal early last year.

In addition to the media situation, Angel Stadium and the area around it are poised for large-scale changes after Kroenke's deal closes early next year. Moreno previously sought to acquire the publicly owned ballpark as part of a more expansive mixed-use development that was planned. The agreement, however, collapsed, in large part due to a corruption investigation of then–Anaheim Mayor Harry Sidhu.

"I feel like it's my birthday," current Anaheim Mayor Ashleigh Aitken told The Athletic. "Not to put the cart ahead of the horse, but if the deal goes through, and if it's approved by Major League Baseball, then I'm very hopeful that [Kroenke is] going to want to work with the city to come up with a really innovative development plan that would benefit the residents. Youth sports fields and housing, and potentially hotel development. And make it a vibrant place."

Angel Stadium is MLB's fourth-oldest ballpark, trailing only iconic venues Fenway Park, Wrigley Field, and Dodger Stadium. Each of those ballparks, and plenty of others, have been dramatically upgraded. Angel Stadium, however, is becoming increasingly outdated and is largely surrounded by surface parking.

Kroenke, meanwhile, has developed SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, and is also creating a mixed-use project in Woodland Hills anchored by the Rams' headquarters and training facility.

Angels icon and future Baseball Hall of Famer Mike Trout cheered the forthcoming ownership transition, saying it was "needed." While Trout has long professed his comfort playing in Anaheim, his talents have been somewhat obscured on a national level because of the Angels' extended losing ways during the Moreno era.

The Angels have already assured themselves of an 11th consecutive losing season in 2026, have not reached the postseason since 2014, and haven't won a playoff game since 2009—two years before Trout made his MLB debut.

"Seeing the reaction from the fans and some of the guys and just the whole vibe, I think it was needed for a fresh start," said Trout, who is under contract through 2030 as part of a 12-year, $426.5 million contract extension signed in 2019. "The biggest thing is getting that winning culture back and having that vibe in the clubhouse."

After hearing the news of the pending sale, Trout called an unnamed Rams player to get his take on Kroenke, and received a positive review. Every one of the major pro sports teams controlled by Kroenke has won a league title under his ownership, and his Rams are the current favorites to win Super Bowl LXI.

"What a track record," Trout said. "Wherever he buys, he wins."

title: Who Will Win the Worst Division Battle in MLB History?
description: The 2026 season of Major League Baseball and its oddities will be looked back on for years to come. There’s an extraordinary power difference between leagues. There could potentially be the first sub-.500 playoff team ever. There’s also a blatantly terrible, yet potentially historic, division race among everything else the 2026 season has challenged.
fullText:
The 2026 season of Major League Baseball and its oddities will be looked back on for years to come.

There's an extraordinary power difference between leagues. There could potentially be the first sub-.500 playoff team ever. There's also a blatantly terrible, yet potentially historic, division race among everything else the 2026 season has challenged.

The American League West can make baseball history in September. The worst division winner ever belongs to the 2005 San Diego Padres. That Bruce Bochy-led club finished 82-80, good enough to take the National League West by five games.

Entering the final month of the MLB season, the Houston Astros lead the AL West with a fragile 70-68 record. They're two full games up on the second-place team, and up five from third-place. That said, given how the wild West has fared, those standings and positions could change or get worse in the blink of an eye.

This division held three .500 teams from the previous season, including one that nearly won the American League. The Seattle Mariners entered as the clear favorite, coming off an ALCS appearance and were one of the premier clubs coming into 2026.

Houston has won the West seven times in the last decade, but is transitioning outside of their dynastic era. However, they're not the most recent team with a World Series in the division. The Texas Rangers bought in and won their only title in franchise history in 2023, but have failed to replicate the magic since. The Astros and Rangers came into the season as potential sleeper teams, but without real postseason aspirations.

The Los Angeles Angels and Athletics were both projected in the basement of the division, stuck in rebuilds. With all of these ambitions set to play out in the Mariners' shadow, nothing has gone as expected.

All five teams have been in first at some point this season. In fact, Seattle has spent some of the least amount of time in first among their division counterparts.

Seattle started slow, giving the Rangers and Athletics space to battle through the first month. Surprisingly enough, the A's either led or were tied for first for 45 straight days starting April 11.

After a 9-1 victory on May 27, the Mariners properly took first and held it. For well over a month, Seattle teetered their record around .500 while keeping the lead. Their governance lasted until the Rangers rode a win streak into July and captured first place for the All-Star break.

The Astros didn't sit idly by for long, taking over the Rangers' spot on July 31. They've led since, but are in no position to begin thinking about October.

This AL West battle between three mediocre teams could be the most exciting story to follow as the season concludes. It's down to the Astros, Rangers and Mariners, who as of Aug. 30 have a combined winning percentage of 48%.

Similar to how the West started with the Mariners, it will end with the Mariners. Over the 24 total games Seattle plays in September, 19 of them are intradivisional. That includes seven games each against the A's and Angels, and one series apiece with the Rangers and Astros.

Oppositely, both Texas and Houston have played the majority of their division series. After a treacherous final month, the Astros embark on a six-game road trip to complete the season. They'll play two games in Seattle and then four in Sacramento against the Athletics.

Texas finishes a home series against the A's to open the month, then visits the Mariners a week later. The Rangers and Astros do not meet in September.

This disordered schedule actually sets up a world where everything could be decided on the final day. On Sept. 27, the Astros play the A's while the Mariners play the Angels. The Rangers travel North and finish their season against the Minnesota Twins, who are also competing for the Wild Card.

All three games would take place at the same time, potentially while delivering baseball history.

Although the Astros have been atop the table since July, the Rangers and Mariners still have a suitable chance.

The biggest obstacle in the Astros' way is not their division opponents, but their schedule itself. Houston plays five clubs that currently hold a playoff spot through the final month. With 24 games remaining, that gives them the 9th hardest strength of schedule. That's by far the most difficult of any team in the AL West.

In the same breath, the Rangers stare down three playoff teams. However, they don't necessarily need to focus on winning the division. As of Aug. 30, they sit two games back from the final Wild Card spot in the American League. There has never been a team outside the extended 2020 playoff format to reach October with a losing record. Texas could become the first if they can't catch the Astros but remain in the race. Or, hell, they could just win the division under .500 and make the postseason regardless.

Do you know which team isn't affected by a hard remaining strength of schedule? The Seattle Mariners. As a matter of fact, they have the easiest in all of baseball. They also have the clear-cut best intradivision record in the AL West. They've gone 20-13 thus far, which suits their division-heavy schedule through September well.

FanGraphs gives Houston a 67% chance to win its eighth division title in the last 10 years. Texas trails with 19%, and Seattle follows with 12%. The trio is projected to finish within three games of each other, furthering the potential of multiple make-or-break series in the final week.

It's that time of the year when every pitch matters. There are about 25 games left, and no team from the West has proved their playoff ready. Or ready to win a division, for that matter.

The beauty of baseball lies in how unpredictable things like this can go. Plus, once you make the playoffs, who knows what could happen.

Will the Astros return to the playoffs, where the core of this roster is all too familiar? Can the Rangers really pursue their second-ever World Series? And when – if at all – will the Mariners die?

The post Who Will Win the Worst Division Battle in MLB History? appeared first on The Lead.

title: Matt Entz has full support and financial backing from Fresno State
description: Matt Entz is getting the support and financial investment he needs at Fresno State. The Bulldogs face USC on Friday
fullText:
Matt Entz is coaching at Fresno State, not Ohio State. He is coaching in the Football Bowl Subdivision's lower realm, not in its top tier, a point which will be magnified when Fresno State faces USC this Friday. Yet, as USA TODAY Sports reports, Entz is getting major investments and backing from his bosses and Fresno State football donors.

"Entz also is embracing the vision of his athletic director, Garrett Klassy, whose previous experience includes Alabama and Houston in upper-cabinet roles. Klassy's vision for Fresno's "Valley Co-Op" has Entz touting a "quadrupled" monetary investment into the Bulldogs' football roster and sees Klassy linking it to the region.

"'I needed coaches, I needed more boots on the street, for lack of a better term, because it couldn't just be myself, it couldn't just be our Bulldog Foundation staff out there,' Klassy says of the program, which he relates to the San Joaquin Valley's 3 million residents and agricultural roots. 'And the coaches, it's really resonated with the coaches, and we do have a lot of supporters that give to multiple programs. There's two areas where we can make up ground on the rest of the league and that's philanthropic giving. And that's corporate sponsorship, and so we need to grow those immensely. And we're going to announce a record fundraising year, which is $5 million more annually than it was the previous year. Corporate sponsorships with the jersey patches are almost across the finish line; we should be up $2 to $3 million in that area. Now that doesn't make a big difference in the SEC or Big Ten, but that makes a huge difference for us.'

Klassy envisions the 4,300-member Valley Co-Op swelling to 7,000 across the next year.

"Entz, meanwhile, wants Fresno football to live up to its billing as the region's top draw.

"'There has been an investment from an administrative standpoint, understanding that we need to have a football program that's good at Fresno State,' said Entz, specifically citing Klassy and Fresno President Dr. Saul Jimenez-Sandoval. 'We have a ton of history and tradition. We're the biggest show in town in the Valley, and people want to see a good product on the field.'"

title: Jim Knowles 'pleased' with Tennessee's continued install progress
description: Jim Knowles discusses Tennessee's defensive install, pass rush ahead of Week 1.
fullText:
Jim Knowles will debut as Tennessee's defensive coordinator on Saturday against Furman (1-0) at Neyland Stadium (3:30 p.m. EDT, SEC Network+).

He was hired to Josh Heupel's staff on Dec. 11, 2025 after coaching the last four seasons in the Big Ten at Ohio State (2022-24) and Penn State (2025).

Ahead of Tennessee's Week 1 contest against Furman, Knowles discussed having continued progress with installation.

"I'm really pleased," Knowles said on Tuesday. "I've found the players to pick things up, to be really diligent in their learning, and very receptive. We brought in some guys that we know and the coaches who know me, that certainly helps, but I think there is a good culture here of learning and I've been impressed with what they've picked up."

"I thought we did well in the preseason," Knowles said. "We're creating some things through various schemes. Not going to get into game planning, but we did some things in fall camp that were effective. I was impressed with what we could generate against our offense, which is a really good offense. Like anything, game time will tell. Game time will tell."

title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a phenomenon – but there is much more to the gaming world
description:
